column5: He releases his grip on my shoulder.{w}\nFor a moment, I was scared things would go south.{w}\nI'm glad that he's so accepting of what transpired.
column6: 他松开了搭在我肩上的手。{w}\n有那么一瞬间，我害怕事情会急转直下。{w}\n我很高兴，他对发生的一切如此坦然接受。

column5: Dropping the issue from my mind, I head up to the deck.{w}\nI had no idea why Damek needed me, but that thought was frightening.{w}\nSlowly ascending the steps, my mind is plagued with unfortunate possibilities.
column6: 我把这事抛到脑后，向甲板走去。{w}\n我不知道达梅克为什么需要我，但这念头令人不安。{w}\n缓缓登上阶梯，种种不祥的可能在脑中挥之不去。

column5: Hey now, put that thing away.\nI didn't mean to startle you, [firstname].
column6: 嘿，别紧张，把那东西收起来。\n我不是有意吓你的，[firstname]。

column5: It's just Vivien. That's a relief.
column6: 只是薇薇安。真是松了口气。

column5: It appears that there's been some... complications.\nDamek wanted me to tell you that you're needed on deck.\nYou'll see what I mean when you get up there, alright?
column6: 似乎出了些……意外状况。\n达梅克让我转告你，甲板上需要你。\n你上去之后就明白我的意思了，好吗？

column5: I nod. It must be important if he's interrupting my rest.{w}\nAs I start to walk away, Vivien puts a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 我点点头。既然他打断我的休息，那一定很重要。{w}\n我正要转身离开，薇薇安把手搭上了我的肩膀。

column5: And I just wanted to tell you that I know what happened in Alarinthia.\nI know that Pro and Ulric teamed up in order to throw our fight.
column6: 我只是想告诉你，我知道阿拉林西亚发生了什么。\n我知道普洛和乌尔里克联手，故意输掉了那场对决。

column5: I gulp, unsure of how Vivien would react to such a news.{w}\nBut much to my surprise, he lets out a hearty laugh.
column6: 我咽了口唾沫，不确定薇薇安听到这个消息会作何反应。{w}\n但出乎我意料的是，他爽朗地笑了起来。

column5: You know, I always said that Alarinthia needed to be ruled with smarts.\nDraycu would just sit in his throne, thinking that strength solved everything.\nUsing a scheme like they did to outsmart him? It's almost poetic, isn't it?
column6: 你知道，我一直说阿拉林西亚需要靠头脑来统治。\n德雷库只会坐在王座上，以为力量能解决一切。\n像他们那样用计谋智取他？简直如诗一般，不是吗？

column5: Besides, it also sent a message to every Alarinthian.\nTheir old way of doing things was wrong. Individual strength doesn't matter.\nIt's how strong we are when we team up — under shared ideals — that truly matters.
column6: 何况，这也给每个阿拉林西亚人传递了一个讯息。\n他们旧日的做法是错的。个人的力量无关紧要。\n真正重要的是，当我们团结在共同的理想之下时，能有多强大。

column5: And for sending them that message, I commend you.\nGood luck out there on the deck. I think you'll need it.
column6: 为了替他们传递这个讯息，我向你致敬。\n甲板上祝你好运。我想你会需要的。

column5: He releases his grip on my shoulder.{w}\nFor a moment, I was scared things would go south.{w}\nI'm glad that he's so accepting of what transpired.
column6: 他松开了搭在我肩上的手。{w}\n有那么一瞬间，我害怕事情会急转直下。{w}\n我很高兴，他对发生的一切如此坦然接受。

column5: Dropping the issue from my mind, I head up to the deck.{w}\nI had no idea why Damek needed me, but that thought was frightening.{w}\nSlowly ascending the steps, my mind is plagued with unfortunate possibilities.
column6: 我把这事抛到脑后，向甲板走去。{w}\n我不知道达梅克为什么需要我，但这念头令人不安。{w}\n缓缓登上阶梯，种种不祥的可能在脑中挥之不去。

column5: As soon as I arrive on the deck, I see exactly why I was needed.{w}\nOff in the distance, we're met by a fleet of ships belonging to The Triumvirate.{w}\nThey're far — but not far enough away that the sheen of the Honor Guard is concealed.
column6: 我一到甲板，就明白为什么需要我了。{w}\n远处，一支属于三人执政团的舰队正与我们相对。{w}\n他们很远——但还没远到能遮住荣誉卫队铠甲的光泽。

column5: Damek and Howl immediately run over. I can see the panic on their faces.{w}\nIt was clear that battle would be imminent. I meet them halfway to see what their plan is.
column6: 达梅克和豪尔立刻跑了过来。我能看到他们脸上的惊慌。{w}\n显然，战斗迫在眉睫。我迎上前去，想听听他们的计划。

column5: We have no plan. \nPerhaps this is time for Damek to shine?\n\"A master strategist\". Is that not what your people say?
column6: 我们没有计划。\n也许现在是达梅克大显身手的时候了？\n“策略大师”。你们那边不是这么说的吗？

column5: Howl, this is no time to be petty.\nWe need to put our heads together and figure this out.\nLet's see — it's a small fleet. Maybe only half the size of ours.
column6: 豪尔，现在不是计较的时候。\n我们得一起动动脑筋，把这事想清楚。\n让我看看——是支小舰队。大概只有我们的一半。

column5: Naval warfare was not something The Monarchy practiced.\nWe lived in peace, Damek. Our world was not discordant like this one.
column6: 海战并非君主国所长。\n我们曾生活在和平之中，达梅克。我们的世界不像这里这般纷乱。

column5: We exchange glances. Damek seems uncertain, and a little worried.{w}\nHe strikes a pose of thought, and it's a while before he breaks the silence.
column6: 我们交换了眼神。达梅克似乎犹豫不决，还有点担忧。{w}\n他摆出沉思的姿态，过了好一会儿才打破沉默。

column5: Okay, I'll do it. We know this battle is lost if [firstname] doesn't make it ashore.\nSo our goal should be securing the safety of this boat, and the lives of those on board.\nThis is when we need to rely on everyone's strengths. We need the Pirates to take action.
column6: 好，我来。我们知道，如果[firstname]不能上岸，这场仗就输了。\n所以我们的目标应该是确保这艘船的安全，以及船上所有人的性命。\n这时候就该依靠每个人的长处。我们需要海盗们出手。

column5: He waves over Alex.
column6: 他招手叫来亚历克斯。

column5: Alex, we need you to order your forces to charge.\nThis is precisely why I wanted to form a treaty. For battle at sea.\nI need you to occupy the forces. Distract them while we slip by.
column6: 亚历克斯，我需要你下令让你的部队冲锋。\n这正是我想缔结条约的原因。为了海战。\n我需要你缠住他们的兵力。在我们溜过去时分散他们的注意力。

column5: Slip by...? They'll notice you right away.\nBaltean ships are equipped with projectile weaponry.\nOne or two good shots and you'll be underwater in minutes.
column6: 溜过去……？他们马上就会发现你们。\n巴尔泰的船都配备了投射武器。\n只要挨上两发好炮，你们几分钟内就会沉进水里。

column5: That's what I'm counting on.
column6: 我正求之不得。

column5: Huh...?
We're going to let them sink this ship.
column6: 我们要让他们把这艘船击沉。

column5: Are you crazy...?
column6: 你疯了吗……？

column5: I have a plan, Alex. Everybody listen up.\nWe'll time it so we're close by when they hit us.\nAs we sink, we can hop over to their ship and hijack it.
column6: 我有计划，亚历克斯。大家听好。\n我们要算好时机，让他们开火时我们就在近旁。\n趁船下沉，我们就能跳到他们的船上，把它夺过来。

column5: Using their own projectile weapons, we'll start sinking them one by one.\nTheir attention will be divided. They'll be getting attacked from multiple sides.\nWe can use that to our advantage. They won't be able to retaliate through the chaos.
column6: 用他们自己的投射武器，我们就能一艘一艘地把他们击沉。\n他们的注意力会被分散，会遭到多方夹击。\n我们可以借此占据上风。混乱之中，他们根本无法还击。

column5: Right, of course.\nShould I send the order right now?
column6: 对，当然。\n我现在就下令吗？

column5: Yeah. We need to do this immediately.\nThere's no room for error. This is the end.
column6: 对。我们必须立刻行动。\n不容有失。这是最后的决战。

column5: Yes, sir!
column6: 是，长官！

column5: Alex runs off and climbs the netting of the ship.{w}\nI look over at the other ships, and pirates start doing the same.{w}\nIt's almost like they have an entire language to communicate over long distances.
column6: 亚历克斯跑开，爬上了船上的网绳。{w}\n我望向其他船只，海盗们也开始做同样的事。{w}\n他们简直像有一套完整的语言，能在远距离互相沟通。

column5: He waves over Nada.
column6: 他招手叫来娜达。

column5: Nada, we need you to order your forces to charge.\nThis is precisely why I wanted to form a treaty. For battle at sea.\nI need you to occupy the forces. Distract them while we slip by.
column6: 娜达，我需要你下令让你的部队冲锋。\n这正是我想缔结条约的原因。为了海战。\n我需要你缠住他们的兵力。在我们溜过去时分散他们的注意力。

column5: Slip by...? They'll notice you right away.\nBaltean ships are equipped with projectile weaponry.\nOne or two good shots and you'll be underwater in minutes.
column6: 溜过去……？他们马上就会发现你们。\n巴尔泰的船都配备了投射武器。\n只要挨上两发好炮，你们几分钟内就会沉进水里。

column5: That's what I'm counting on.
column6: 我正求之不得。

column5: Excuse me...?
column6: 你说什么……？

column5: We're going to let them sink this ship.
column6: 我们要让他们把这艘船击沉。

column5: You can't be serious.
column6: 你不是认真的吧。

column5: I have a plan, Nada. Everybody listen up.\nWe'll time it so we're close by when they hit us.\nAs we sink, we can hop over to their ship and hijack it.
column6: 我有计划，娜达。大家听好。\n我们要算好时机，让他们开火时我们就在近旁。\n趁船下沉，我们就能跳到他们的船上，把它夺过来。

column5: Using their own projectile weapons, we'll start sinking them one by one.\nTheir attention will be divided. They'll be getting attacked from multiple sides.\nWe can use that to our advantage. They won't be able to retaliate through the chaos.
column6: 用他们自己的投射武器，我们就能一艘一艘地把他们击沉。\n他们的注意力会被分散，会遭到多方夹击。\n我们可以借此占据上风。混乱之中，他们根本无法还击。

column5: A bold move, you know.\nDo you want me to send the order...?
column6: 这可是大胆的一步。\n要我下令吗……？

column5: Yeah. We need to do this immediately.\nThere's no room for error. This is the end.
column6: 对。我们必须立刻行动。\n不容有失。这是最后的决战。

column5: Sure thing.
column6: 没问题。

column5: Nada runs off and climbs the netting of the ship.{w}\nI look over at the other ships, and pirates start doing the same.{w}\nIt's almost like they have an entire language to communicate over long distances.
column6: 娜达跑开，爬上了船上的网绳。{w}\n我望向其他船只，海盗们也开始做同样的事。{w}\n他们简直像有一套完整的语言，能在远距离互相沟通。

column5: That was an impressive sight to see.{w}\nHowever, seeing Damek think on his feet was equally impressive.{w}\nWith a sigh and a smile, confidence overtakes the panic from moments before.
column6: 那景象着实令人叹为观止。{w}\n不过，看着达梅克临机应变，同样令人钦佩。{w}\n随着一声叹息和一抹微笑，信心压过了片刻前的惊慌。

column5: Damek. We must say, that was pretty impressive.\nHopefully now you realize that visions only hold you back.
column6: 达梅克。我们得说，那相当了得。\n但愿你现在明白，预知只会束缚你。

column5: Huh...?
Look at what happened back in the Rebel HQ.\nYou relied on a vision. You tried to fulfill some prophecy.\nIn a way, that is limiting. You plan your strategy around certainties.
column6: 想想在反抗军总部发生的事。\n你依赖预知，试图实现某个预言。\n某种程度上，那是一种束缚。你围绕着确定之事来制定策略。

column5: But there are no certainties in war.\nAssume that the enemy has a counter for your every action.\nIn this case — we should also plan for a scenario where the enemy prevails.
column6: 但战争中没有什么确定之事。\n要假设敌人对你们的每个行动都有应对之策。\n就这次而言——我们也该为敌人获胜的情形做好准备。

column5: Damek shakes his head.
column6: 达梅克摇了摇头。

column5: They won't. Simply because we can't afford it.\nAny losses at this point would mean the end of our cause.\nTrust in the Pirates, Howl. Trust in all of us. We can do this.
column6: 他们不会赢。只因为我们输不起。\n此刻任何损失都意味着我们事业的终结。\n相信海盗们，豪尔。相信我们所有人。我们能行。

column5: Howl simply nods. Moments later, the pirates launch their assault.{w}\nWe all lose our balance as our ship takes a sharp turn, moving in a new direction.{w}\nThis was a risky plan, but like Damek requested, I chose to place my trust in him.
column6: 豪尔只是点了点头。片刻之后，海盗们发起了进攻。{w}\n船猛地一转，驶向新的方向，我们全都失去了平衡。{w}\n这是个冒险的计划，但正如达梅克所请，我选择相信他。

column5: If trust wouldn't carry us to victory, then it would be our strength and resolve.{w}\nI hold on to the side of the ship as our speed increases. Everybody braces themselves.{w}\nThey're not sure what's going on, so Damek draws his sword and raises it into the air.
column6: 如果信任不能带我们走向胜利，那就靠我们的力量与决心。{w}\n船速渐增，我紧紧抓住船舷。所有人都绷紧了身体。{w}\n他们不清楚发生了什么，于是达梅克拔出剑，高高举向空中。

column5: Everybody, listen up! The final hour is upon us.\nOur Pirate army will be charging against the enemy fleet.\nWhile they're distracted, we'll slip in and hijack one of their ships.
column6: 各位，听好！最后的时刻到了。\n我们的海盗大军将向敌方舰队发起冲锋。\n在他们被牵制时，我们就溜进去，夺下他们的一艘船。

column5: That means we'll be sacrificing this vessel.\nSo don't be alarmed if they deal us a fatal blow.\nAs we're sinking, we'll jump over and board the enemy.
column6: 也就是说，我们要牺牲这艘船。\n所以就算他们给我们致命一击，也不要惊慌。\n船下沉时，我们就跳过去登上敌舰。

column5: Their ships are equipped with projectile weaponry.\nUsing their own ship, we will turn their weapons against them.\nThey won't know where to focus, and we'll use the chaos to our advantage.
column6: 他们的船上装备了投射武器。\n用他们自己的船，我们要让他们的武器反过来对付他们。\n他们会不知道该把火力集中在哪里，我们就利用这场混乱占得上风。

column5: He starts to talk a bit louder as our ship picks up speed.{w}\nWe move away from the main fleet, preparing to approach from the flank.{w}\nI notice the soldiers nod, accepting Damek's orders and plan without hesitation.
column6: 随着船速加快，他提高了嗓门。{w}\n我们驶离主舰队，准备从侧翼逼近。{w}\n我注意到士兵们纷纷点头，毫不犹豫地接受了达梅克的命令和计划。

column5: If things go south, I need all of you to protect [firstname]. \nWithout him, we will lose not only this battle, but the war as well.\nHis life, and the blade that he carries, should be our top priority.
column6: 如果情况不妙，我需要你们所有人保护[firstname]。\n没有他，我们不仅会输掉这场战斗，还会输掉整场战争。\n他的性命，以及他携带的那把剑，必须是我们最优先保护的东西。

column5: If things go south, I need all of you to protect [firstname].\nWithout her, we will lose not only this battle, but the war as well.\nHer life, and the blade that she carries, should be our top priority.
column6: 如果情况不妙，我需要你们所有人保护[firstname]。\n没有她，我们不仅会输掉这场战斗，还会输掉整场战争。\n她的性命，以及她携带的那把剑，必须是我们最优先保护的东西。

column5: Do I make myself clear!?
column6: 我说清楚了吗！？

column5: Everybody cheers in approval, and raises their sword like Damek.{w}\nThen, we all stand and watch the bulk of our fleet as the battle begins.{w}\nWe slowly move away from the action, and I can tell that some are relieved.
column6: 众人齐声欢呼赞同，像达梅克那样举起了剑。{w}\n随后，战斗打响，我们全都站着望向舰队主力。{w}\n我们缓缓驶离战场，我能看出有些人松了口气。

column5: As soon as the pirates get close enough, The Honor Guard retaliates.{w}\nThey launch heavy projectiles from catapults, and shoot harpoons from wooden structures.{w}\nThe pirates, with their sailing expertise, are mostly able to counter by altering their trajectory.
column6: 海盗们刚一靠近，荣誉卫队就展开了反击。{w}\n他们用投石机发射沉重的弹丸，从木制结构上射出鱼叉。{w}\n海盗们凭借精湛的航海本领，大多能通过改变航向来应对。

column5: However, not all of them can do so. I witness several ships get torn apart and start to sink.{w}\nMy heart sinks with them, knowing that they were willing to sacrifice themselves for {i}me{/i}.{w}\nIt seems that the battle is on in full force. They get closer, and start to board each other.
column6: 然而，并非所有人都能做到。我眼看着好几艘船被撕裂，开始下沉。{w}\n我的心也随之沉了下去，因为我知道他们甘愿为{i}我{/i}牺牲。{w}\n战斗似乎已全面展开。双方越靠越近，开始互相登船厮杀。

column5: I can hear swords clashing as The Honor Guard tries to defend against the pirates' charge.{w}\nShips on both sides start to sink, and soon enough, it's almost impossible to see what's happening.{w}\nFrom this distance, it's too chaotic. But if enemy ships are sinking, we must've seized some weapons.
column6: 伴随着荣誉卫队抵抗海盗冲锋的厮杀声，我能听见刀剑相交。{w}\n双方的船只都开始下沉，很快，几乎看不出战况如何。{w}\n从这个距离看，一切太过混乱。但既然敌舰在沉没，我们一定已经夺下了一些武器。

column5: That means the tables have started to turn. But it's up to us to play our part, as well.{w}\nI turn back and look at where we're headed. We're dangerously close to some enemy ships.{w}\nDamek calls out to everybody, shifting their attention away from the distant battle.
column6: 这意味着局势开始逆转。但也得靠我们演好自己这一出。{w}\n我回头看了看我们前进的方向。我们已危险地逼近几艘敌舰。{w}\n达梅克高声呼喊众人，把他们的注意力从远处的战斗上拉了回来。

column5: This is it. There is {i}no{/i} turning back...!\nEverybody brace yourselves to charge!
column6: 就是现在。已经{i}没有{/i}回头路了……！\n所有人做好准备，准备冲锋！

column5: I can see The Honor Guard prepare their weapons.{w}\nWhen I scan my surroundings, I can see our forces prepare as well.{w}\nA line of archers forms, ready to attack the enemies at a moment's notice.
column6: 我能看到荣誉卫队在准备武器。{w}\n环顾四周，我看到我们的部队也在准备。{w}\n一排弓箭手列好阵型，随时准备向敌人发动攻击。

column5: Hold...!
column6: 稳住……！

column5: He places a fist in the air. An intense silence follows.{w}\nBoth sides are armed. The question is, who attacks first...?{w}\nI take a deep breath, and pull out The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 他把拳头举向空中。随之而来的是死一般的寂静。{w}\n双方都已持械。问题是，谁会先出手……？{w}\n我深吸一口气，拔出了流亡之刃。

column5: Hold...!
column6: 稳住……！

column5: I look over at the ships we've left behind. The numbers are easily halved.{w}\nBut this goes for the enemy as well. This was clearly the turning point.{w}\nWhat happened next would decide the fate of our entire cause.
column6: 我望向我们身后的那些船。数量显然已减半。{w}\n但敌人也一样。这显然就是转折点。{w}\n接下来发生的事，将决定我们整个事业的命运。

column5: And it began with a barrage of projectile weaponry.{w}\nThe enemy attacked our ship with everything they had.{w}\nI can feel the hull get torn apart, and everything starts shaking.
column6: 而它始于一场投射武器的齐射。{w}\n敌人倾尽所有攻击我们的船。{w}\n我能感觉到船体被撕裂，一切都开始晃动。

column5: Fire...!
column6: 开火……！

column5: The archers return fire, knocking out the suits of armor manning the weapons.{w}\nI look back at the wheel of the ship, and Alex spins it, turning us toward the enemy vessels.
column6: 弓箭手们还击，击倒了操作武器的铠甲兵。{w}\n我回头看向船舵，亚历克斯转动舵轮，让船转向敌舰。

column5: I hope you're ready to jump...!
column6: 希望你准备好跳了……！

column5: The archers return fire, knocking out the suits of armor manning the weapons.{w}\nI look back at the wheel of the ship, and Nada spins it, turning us toward the enemy vessels.
column6: 弓箭手们还击，击倒了操作武器的铠甲兵。{w}\n我回头看向船舵，娜达转动舵轮，让船转向敌舰。

column5: This is it. Get ready to jump...!
column6: 就是现在。准备跳……！

column5: Damek nods, and then a moment later, everything erupts into chaos.{w}\nOur forces jump to the enemy ship, after a long running start.{w}\nThey land safely, and start decimating The Honor Guard.
column6: 达梅克点了点头，片刻之后，一切都陷入了混乱。{w}\n我们的部队经过长距离助跑，跳上了敌舰。{w}\n他们安全落地，开始大肆屠戮荣誉卫队。

column5: See you on the other side, [firstname].
column6: 另一边见，[firstname]。

column5: With a smirk, he follows our soldiers, jumping across to the enemy ship.{w}\nLanding with a roll, he immediately starts fighting, displaying impressive skill.{w}\nI didn't get to see him fight in our HQ {i}or{/i} in Alarinthia. It's quite the sight.
column6: 他咧嘴一笑，跟着我们的士兵跳向敌舰。{w}\n他就地一滚落地，立刻投入战斗，展现出惊人的身手。{w}\n我在总部{i}和{/i}阿拉林西亚都没机会看他出手。这景象真是难得。

column5: He dodges the enemy attacks with ease, and retaliates with expertise.{w}\nTaking out multiple suits of armor with a single swing, he clearly holds his own.{w}\nI turn around, and order the remaining soldiers to charge. I save myself for last.
column6: 他轻松闪避敌人的攻击，以娴熟的技巧还击。{w}\n一挥剑就击倒好几具铠甲兵，显然游刃有余。{w}\n我转过身，命令剩下的士兵冲锋。我把自己留到最后。

column5: But before I jump, I notice that Alex is still at the wheel.{w}\nI shout his name, and tell him to get across as soon as possible.{w}\nThe ship has already started to sink — and water rises at my feet.
column6: 但在我起跳之前，我注意到亚历克斯还在舵轮旁。{w}\n我大喊他的名字，让他尽快过去。{w}\n船已经开始下沉——水漫到了我的脚边。

column5: You know — any good Captain is supposed to go down with their ship.\nBut I guess there's no point living my life by an outdated code of honor.\nThanks to the treaty, there'll be a new life waiting for me after all of this.
column6: 你知道——好船长本该与自己的船一同沉没。\n但我想，按过时的荣誉准则过日子也没什么意义。\n多亏了那份条约，这一切结束后，会有新生活在等着我。

column5: He leaves the wheel behind, and places a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 他离开舵轮，把手搭在我的肩上。

column5: And honestly, it's all thanks to you.\nLet's make this jump together, [firstname].\nWe're a team until the end. No matter what.
column6: 说实话，这全都要感谢你。\n我们一起跳吧，[firstname]。\n我们是同生共死的伙伴。无论如何。

column5: No matter what.
column6: 无论如何。

column5: We move to the opposite side of the ship, putting distance between us and the enemy vessel.{w}\nI notice that most of The Honor Guard has fallen, and our soldiers are manning the weaponry.{w}\nThat's a good sign. With a feeling that victory is ours, Alex and I start to sprint toward the enemy.
column6: 我们移动到船的另一侧，与敌舰拉开距离。{w}\n我注意到荣誉卫队大多已经倒下，我们的士兵正在操作武器。{w}\n这是个好兆头。怀着胜利在望的感觉，我和亚历克斯开始向敌人冲刺。

column5: He makes it there first, jumping up on the railing of our ship and lauching himself across the gap.{w}\nI'm not too far behind, and I jump up on the railing moments after. However, I make it no further.{w}\nAn arrow pierces through my shoulder, and I fall back onto our ship, in a pool of freezing water.
column6: 他先到了那里，跳上我们船的栏杆，腾身越过空隙。{w}\n我紧随其后，片刻后也跳上栏杆。然而，我再也无法向前。{w}\n一支箭射穿了我的肩膀，我跌回自己的船上，落在冰冷的水洼里。

column5: But before I jump, I notice that Nada is still at the wheel.{w}\nI shout her name, and tell her to get across as soon as possible.{w}\nThe ship has already started to sink — and water rises at my feet.
column6: 但在我起跳之前，我注意到娜达还在舵轮旁。{w}\n我大喊她的名字，让她尽快过去。{w}\n船已经开始下沉——水漫到了我的脚边。

column5: You know, the code of honor states that a Captain should go down with her ship.\nIf it weren't for that treaty, I'd be ready to let myself die right here and now.\nI think my new nation will change things up a bit. No more stupid sacrifices.
column6: 你知道，荣誉准则规定船长应当与自己的船一同沉没。\n要不是那份条约，我此刻就甘愿死在这里。\n我想我的新国家会有所改变。不再有愚蠢的牺牲。

column5: She leaves the wheel behind, and places a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 她离开舵轮，把手搭在我的肩上。

column5: I have to thank you for what you've done, [firstname].\nNow let's make this jump — there's still so much left to do.
column6: 我得谢谢你做的一切，[firstname]。\n现在我们一起跳吧——还有很多事要做。

column5: A sly smirk appears on her face.
column6: 她脸上浮现出一抹狡黠的笑。

column5: Hey — first one there gets more suits to kill. \nDon't want to keep them waiting, right?
column6: 嘿——先到的人能多杀几具铠甲。\n可别让他们等太久，对吧？

column5: We move to the opposite side of the ship, putting distance between us and the enemy vessel.{w}\nI notice that most of The Honor Guard has fallen, and our soldiers are manning the weaponry.{w}\nThat's a good sign. With a feeling that victory is ours, Nada and I start to sprint toward the enemy.
column6: 我们移动到船的另一侧，与敌舰拉开距离。{w}\n我注意到荣誉卫队大多已经倒下，我们的士兵正在操作武器。{w}\n这是个好兆头。怀着胜利在望的感觉，我和娜达开始向敌人冲刺。

column5: She makes it there first, jumping up on the railing of our ship and lauching himself across the gap.{w}\nI'm not too far behind, and I jump up on the railing moments after. However, I make it no further.{w}\nAn arrow pierces through my shoulder, and I fall back onto our ship, in a pool of freezing water.
column6: 她先到了那里，跳上我们船的栏杆，腾身越过空隙。{w}\n我紧随其后，片刻后也跳上栏杆。然而，我再也无法向前。{w}\n一支箭射穿了我的肩膀，我跌回自己的船上，落在冰冷的水洼里。

column5: I pull out the arrow with a grunt. Blood oozes from the wound, but it's nothing major.{w}\nWe could patch it up as soon as the enemy ships were taken care of. I rise to my feet.{w}\nLooking up, I immediately notice the source of the arrow. It wasn't The Honor Guard.
column6: 我闷哼一声拔出了箭。血从伤口渗出，但不算严重。{w}\n等解决完敌舰，就能马上包扎。我站起身来。{w}\n抬头一看，我立刻注意到箭是从哪来的。那不是荣誉卫队。

column5: It was Shane.
column6: 是肖恩。

column5: With an evil smirk, he jumps across, boarding our ship. It's still sinking, but I have time.{w}\nIf I can take care of him fast enough, then I'd be able to carry out my plan as originally intended.{w}\nInstead of coming for me, he runs toward the wheel, steering our ship away from the chaos.
column6: 他带着邪恶的笑意跳了过来，登上了我们的船。船还在下沉，但我还有时间。{w}\n只要我能足够快地解决他，就能按原计划行事。{w}\n他没有朝我来，而是跑向舵轮，把我们的船驶离混乱。

column5: That wasn't good. My time was limited if we were both sinking and making the distance greater.{w}\nHe must know exactly what he's doing. Part of me wonders if we played into some sort of trap.{w}\nI look at my allies, and they seem to be doing a good enough job as they enact our plan.
column6: 这可不妙。如果双方都在下沉，距离又越来越远，我的时间就有限了。{w}\n他一定清楚自己在做什么。我有些怀疑我们是不是落入了某种陷阱。{w}\n我看向同伴们，他们执行计划时似乎做得还不错。

column5: My fist shakes as I grip The Blade of Exodus. Shane scoffs as he watches.{w}\nI shout at him in anger and despair. I call him a traitor, and condemn him.{w}\nHe almost killed Damek. He caused irreparable damage to my family...!
column6: 我紧握着流亡之刃，拳头在颤抖。肖恩看着，嗤笑了一声。{w}\n我带着愤怒与绝望对他大喊，骂他是叛徒，谴责他。{w}\n他差点杀了达梅克。他给我的家人造成了无法弥补的伤害……！

column5: A traitor...!? Not from where I'm standing.\nDamek abandoned {i}me{/i}, and it's all because of you!\nHe's a selfish fool. All he cares about is that stupid sword...!
column6: 叛徒……！？在我眼里可不是这样。\n达梅克抛弃了{i}我{/i}，全都是因为你！\n他是个自私的蠢货。他在乎的只有那把破剑……！

column5: I keep walking toward him, and the ship shakes violently.{w}\nWater keeps spilling on the deck, and I'm standing almost ankle-deep.
column6: 我继续朝他走去，船剧烈地摇晃着。{w}\n水不断涌上甲板，我站着时水几乎没过了脚踝。

column5: I had a plan. {i}We{/i} had a plan...! And he threw it all away.\nThe moment you walked through that door, he let you replace me.\nHe left me to rot in The Triumvirate's prison because you were more convenient.
column6: 我有个计划。{i}我们{/i}有个计划……！而他把它全扔了。\n你走进那扇门的那一刻，他就让你取代了我。\n他把我丢在三人执政团的监狱里烂掉，因为用你更方便。

column5: That's not true! I try and reason with Shane, but to no avail.
column6: 不是那样的！我试着跟肖恩讲理，但毫无作用。

column5: You saw how many people died in your HQ during that little attack.\nIf you couldn't wield that sword, you'd be buried down there with the rest of them!\nDamek didn't care about you, or your friends. He only cared about your power.
column6: 你看到了那次小规模袭击中，你的总部死了多少人。\n要是你握不了那把剑，你早就和他们一起埋在那里了！\n达梅克根本不在乎你，也不在乎你的朋友。他只在乎你的力量。

column5: Again, that's not true! He's clearly been converted by The Triumvirate.
column6: 再说一次，不是那样的！他显然已经被三人执政团策反了。

column5: I was thinking long and hard about what I should do.\nYou know — what was my place in all of this...?
column6: 我一直在苦苦思索自己该怎么做。\n你知道——我在这一切之中，究竟算什么……？

column5: Much to my surprise, he throws both of his daggers on the ground.
column6: 让我意外的是，他把两把匕首都扔在了地上。

column5: And I realized that if I served The Triumvirate, I'd receive the same power.\nIt seemed fitting. End Damek's rebellion with the same thing he was relying on.
column6: 然后我意识到，如果我效忠三人执政团，就能获得同样的力量。\n这似乎很合适。用达梅克所依赖的同一件东西，终结他的叛乱。

column5: He smirks, and I can tell that the man Damek cared about was already dead.
column6: 他笑了笑，我明白达梅克所珍视的那个人，早已不在了。

column5: I wish he could be here to see this.\nBut you'll tell him the story — won't you?
column6: 真希望他能在这儿亲眼看看。\n但你会把这段故事讲给他听的——对吧？

column5: A moment later, he charges at me, unarmed.{w}\nBut in almost the blink of an eye, the blade appears in his hands.{w}\nRobbed from mine, I have no choice but to jump out of the way.
column6: 片刻之后，他赤手空拳地朝我冲来。{w}\n但几乎就在眨眼之间，那把剑出现在了他手中。{w}\n我的剑被夺走，别无选择，只能闪身避开。

column5: I run to the opposite side of the ship, where he threw his pair of daggers.{w}\nPicking them up, I assume a fighting stance, and wait for him to charge again.
column6: 我跑到船的另一侧，也就是他扔掉那对匕首的地方。{w}\n我捡起匕首，摆出战斗姿态，等着他再次冲来。

column5: Not strong enough to take it back by willpower alone...?\nThought so. You're weak. See, I was blessed by The Triumvirate.\nAll you got was worthless energy from the realm of spirits. Out of pity, too.
column6: 光靠意志力没本事把它夺回去……？\n我就知道。你很弱。看吧，我得到了三人执政团的赐福。\n你得到的只是来自灵界的一文不值的能量。而且还是出于怜悯。

column5: He doesn't seem to know about the Monarchy, or the true nature of the power within me.{w}\nBig surprise. The Triumvirate lost Sovy when he found out. I should use this to my advantage.{w}\nAs he charges, I maintain the facade that I'm weak and unable to summon back the blade.
column6: 他似乎并不知道君主国的事，也不了解我体内力量的真正本质。{w}\n毫不意外。索维发现真相后，三人执政团就失去了他。我该利用这一点。{w}\n他冲来时，我继续装作软弱无力，无法唤回那把剑。

column5: I dodge to the side once more, but slice into Shane's arm with one of his own daggers.{w}\nHe winces and grunts. His arm starts to bleed, but it doesn't seem to affect his performance.{w}\nHe charges again, and I dodge to the other side. With a roll, I slice into his leg. He stumbles.
column6: 我再次侧身闪避，用他自己的一把匕首划伤了肖恩的手臂。{w}\n他皱起脸，闷哼一声。手臂开始流血，但似乎没影响他的动作。{w}\n他又冲了过来，我向另一侧闪避。一个翻滚，我划中了他的腿。他脚步踉跄。

column5: I have speed and agility, while he relies on slow, brute strength.{w}\nIt's easy to tell that he's never fought with such a weapon before.{w}\nFrom what I've seen, he can really only use arrows and daggers.
column6: 我速度快、身手灵，而他只靠迟缓的蛮力。{w}\n很容易看出，他从没用过这种武器作战。{w}\n据我所见，他真正会使的只有弓箭和匕首。

column5: Is that all you've got...?
column6: 你就这点本事……？

column5: I won't be able to keep up the same strategy forever.{w}\nI'd need to change it up while I think of how to end this.{w}\nHe charges once more, but this time, I meet him head on.
column6: 我不可能一直用同样的策略。{w}\n我得换个打法，同时想想怎么结束这一切。{w}\n他又一次冲来，但这一次，我正面迎了上去。

column5: Holding out the daggers in a cross formation, I stop the blade from going any further.{w}\nWe struggle, both at almost equal strength, trembling as we try to overpower the other.{w}\nI tell Shane that Damek is still alive. The spirits willed it because his cause was righteous.
column6: 我交叉举起匕首，架住了那把剑，让它无法再进一步。{w}\n我们较着力，力量几乎不相上下，都颤抖着想压过对方。{w}\n我告诉肖恩，达梅克还活着。因为他的事业是正义的，所以灵界让他活了下来。

column5: Impossible...!
column6: 不可能……！

column5: He'd never comply if I told him to look for himself, so there's no way I can prove it.{w}\nHowever, he seems to let up a little bit, and I'm able to overpower him some more.{w}\nI push him away, and tell him that it's all true. He's on the wrong side of this war.
column6: 就算我叫他自己去看，他也绝不会照做，所以我根本无法证明。{w}\n然而，他似乎稍微松懈了些，我得以再占几分上风。{w}\n我把他推开，告诉他这都是真的。他站错了这场战争的边。

column5: No! You're the one on the wrong side!\nThe Rebellion is small and insignificant...!\nHundreds, standing in a world of millions.
column6: 不！站错边的人是你！\n反抗军又小又不值一提……！\n几百人，对抗一个数百万人的世界。

column5: Even if you win, they won't respect your power!\nThey're {i}happy{/i} living under The Triumvirate's rule.\nRevenge won't solve anything. Just back down...!
column6: 就算你赢了，他们也不会敬畏你的力量！\n他们{i}心甘情愿{/i}活在三人执政团的统治下。\n复仇解决不了任何问题。退让吧……！

column5: We circle around each other, both holding out our weapons.
column6: 我们举着武器，绕着彼此转圈。

column5: I was hurt by The Occupation, and I wanted to fight.\nBut I realized I was being greedy; and there was no point.\nIt's not my happiness — my satisfaction, that matters. It's the world's.
column6: 我曾因占领而受伤，我想战斗。\n但我意识到那只是我的贪念，毫无意义。\n重要的不是我的幸福——我的满足。而是这个世界的。

column5: It seems we've reached a stalemate — both trying to talk each other down.{w}\nBut I wouldn't yield, and something told me that he wouldn't either.{w}\nHis views have been twisted; and he thinks mine have as well.
column6: 看来我们陷入了僵局——都想说服对方放弃。{w}\n但我不会让步，而我有种感觉，他也不会。{w}\n他的观念已被扭曲；而他认为我的也是。

column5: We charge at each other, and meet in the middle once more.{w}\nThe water rises, and I can tell that time is minimal. We're sinking fast.{w}\nReturning to the same deadlock as before, I'd need to do {i}something{/i}.
column6: 我们互相冲去，再次在中央相遇。{w}\n水在上涨，我明白时间不多了。船下沉得很快。{w}\n又回到了和之前一样的僵持，我必须做点{i}什么{/i}。

column5: I'd need to summon the blade back when he least expects it.{w}\nMy time is limited, and it honestly seems like Shane is beyond saving.{w}\nBut the question is — what do I do when it's back in my grasp...?
column6: 我得在他最意想不到的时候把剑召回来。{w}\n我的时间有限，而且说实话，肖恩似乎已经无可救药。{w}\n但问题是——当剑回到我手中，我该怎么做……？

column5: I have to kill him. It's the only way.{w}\nOtherwise, he'd continue to be a thorn in our side.{w}\nWe couldn't afford any potential disruptions. Not anymore.
column6: 我必须杀了他。这是唯一的办法。{w}\n否则，他会继续成为我们的眼中钉。{w}\n我们再也经不起任何潜在的干扰了。不能再有了。

column5: You took everything from me...!
column6: 你夺走了我的一切……！

column5: As his anger and rage empowers him, I start to tremble even more.{w}\nIt takes a lot to resist the strength of a man wielding The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 随着愤怒与狂暴为他注入力量，我开始颤抖得更厉害。{w}\n要抵挡一个手握流亡之刃之人的力量，需要极大的力气。

column5: You were born with everything I worked so hard to achieve...!\nThey were my family — my friends! And you took them all away!
column6: 你生来就拥有我拼命奋斗才得到的一切……！\n他们是我的家人——我的朋友！而你把他们全都夺走了！

column5: As he starts to get more desperate and angry, I decide to take action.{w}\nI let him overpower me, and I step to the side, dodging his next swing.
column6: 随着他越发绝望和愤怒，我决定采取行动。{w}\n我让他压过我，然后侧身一闪，避开了他接下来的挥砍。

column5: I hate you...!
column6: 我恨你……！

column5: But immediately after, and much to his surprise, I phase the blade back into my hands.{w}\nTurning back toward him, I thrust the blade through his abdomen, and push him back.{w}\nHe lets out a scream as I pull it back out, and he stumbles back, clutching the wound.
column6: 但紧接着，出乎他意料的是，我把剑瞬间召回手中。{w}\n我转向他，将剑刺入他的腹部，把他推了回去。{w}\n我拔出剑时，他发出一声惨叫，踉跄后退，捂住伤口。

column5: He realizes I was lying, and fooled him. He says nothing, and drops to his knees.{w}\nI watch as he seems to fade in and out of consciousness, wobbling back and forth.{w}\nMuttering his final words as he slumps back, he lands in a pool of water that soon tints red.
column6: 他意识到我骗了他，耍了他。他什么也没说，跪倒在地。{w}\n我看着他似乎在清醒与昏迷之间浮沉，身子前后摇晃。{w}\n他瘫倒下去，喃喃着最后的话，倒进一汪水洼，那水很快染上了红色。

column5: Damek...
column6: 达梅克……

column5: I had to get moving, and fast...!{w}\nThis encounter was enough of a distraction.{w}\nI give him a moment of silence before making my escape.
column6: 我得走了，而且要快……！{w}\n这场遭遇已经拖得够久了。{w}\n我为他默哀片刻，然后逃离了那里。

column5: He didn't deserve to die, that much was clear.{w}\nThere had to be a chance that he'd see reason in the future.{w}\nIf I went on to win this war, maybe he'd see things differently.
column6: 他不该死，这一点很明确。{w}\n将来总该有一丝可能，让他明白道理。{w}\n如果我能赢得这场战争，也许他会换个角度看事情。

column5: You took everything from me...!
column6: 你夺走了我的一切……！

column5: As his anger and rage empowers him, I start to tremble even more.{w}\nIt takes a lot to resist the strength of a man wielding The Blade of Exodus.{w}\nI do my best to buy time until I find the right opportunity. I contest Shane's words.
column6: 随着愤怒与狂暴为他注入力量，我开始颤抖得更厉害。{w}\n要抵挡一个手握流亡之刃之人的力量，需要极大的力气。{w}\n我尽力拖延时间，等待合适的时机。我反驳肖恩的话。

column5: You were born with everything I worked so hard to achieve...!\nThey were my family — my friends! And you took them all away!
column6: 你生来就拥有我拼命奋斗才得到的一切……！\n他们是我的家人——我的朋友！而你把他们全都夺走了！

column5: As he starts to get more desperate and angry, I decide to take action.{w}\nI let him overpower me, and I step to the side, dodging his next swing.
column6: 随着他越发绝望和愤怒，我决定采取行动。{w}\n我让他压过我，然后侧身一闪，避开了他接下来的挥砍。

column5: I hate you...!
column6: 我恨你……！

column5: But immediately after, and much to his surprise, I phase the blade back into my hands.{w}\nWhile he's caught off guard, I raise the blade in the air, and smash the base against his head.{w}\nHe screams and stumbles back, knocked into a daze. I step forward, and do the same thing again.
column6: 但紧接着，出乎他意料的是，我把剑瞬间召回手中。{w}\n趁他猝不及防，我举起剑，用剑柄砸向他的头。{w}\n他惨叫着踉跄后退，被打得头晕眼花。我上前一步，又做了同样的事。

column5: I'm careful not to go too far, and I stop the moment I find enough time to make my escape.{w}\nHe slumps down on the ground, almost knocked unconscious. I can hear him cry and whimper.{w}\nThere was no way to know if he'd make it out of this alive, but at least the had a chance.
column6: 我小心不做得太过，一找到足够逃脱的时机就停了手。{w}\n他瘫倒在地上，几乎失去意识。我能听见他哭泣和呜咽。{w}\n无法确定他能否活着挺过去，但至少他还有机会。

column5: Damek...
column6: 达梅克……

column5: This was enough of a distraction. I had to get moving!{w}\nLooking back at Shane, it's crushing how far he seems to have fallen.{w}\nWhen I saw Damek again, it might be wise not to even tell him what happened.
column6: 这已经拖得够久了。我得走了！{w}\n回头看向肖恩，他堕落得如此之深，令人心碎。{w}\n等我再见到达梅克时，也许最好连发生了什么都别告诉他。

column5: I jump in the water, and immediately start swimming toward the ship my comrades are on.{w}\nBut soon after jumping in, the freezing water makes my limbs feel stiff, and my chest heavy.{w}\nFighting it for as long as I can, I keep swimming. I know I can do this...! This is {i}no{/i} time to give up!
column6: 我跳进水里，立刻朝同伴们所在的船游去。{w}\n但入水不久，冰冷的水让我的四肢变得僵硬，胸口沉重。{w}\n我拼命抵抗着，不停向前游。我知道我能做到……！这{i}绝不是{/i}放弃的时候！

column5: When my vision fades back in, I can feel that I'm being dragged. What happened?{w}\nMy body is covered in snow, and I'm shivering. I must've passed out back in the water.{w}\nI shake my head, and whoever is carrying me seems to notice. They put me down and sigh.
column6: 当我恢复视觉时，我能感觉到自己正被拖行。发生了什么？{w}\n我浑身是雪，瑟瑟发抖。我一定是在水里昏了过去。{w}\n我摇了摇头，背着我的人似乎察觉到了。他把我放下，叹了口气。

column5: You're awake. Thank goodness.\nWhen I found you in the water, I was starting to worry.\nWhat happened back there, anyway? You were so far behind us.
column6: 你醒了。谢天谢地。\n我在水里发现你的时候，都开始担心了。\n到底发生了什么？你落后我们那么远。

column5: I shake my head, telling him that I can't remember much. A necessary lie.{w}\nIf he knew what Shane tried to do, and how lost he was — it would damage his morale.{w}\nHe needed to see my survival as a triumph. We couldn't afford any damaged morale.
column6: 我摇摇头，告诉他我记不太清了。这是个必要的谎言。{w}\n如果他知道肖恩想做什么，以及他迷失得有多深——那会打击他的士气。{w}\n他需要把我的生还看作一场胜利。我们经不起士气受损。

column5: Oh, I see. Can you stand on your own?\nWe're resting in a shack that's not too far away.\nIt's nothing fancy — but it'll give us the privacy we need.
column6: 哦，我明白了。你能自己站起来吗？\n我们就在不远处的一间小屋里歇脚。\n不算讲究——但能给我们需要的那份清静。

column5: Nodding, I get up on my feet.{w}\nI stumble a bit, but Damek can tell I'm still fine.
column6: 我点点头，站了起来。{w}\n我踉跄了一下，但达梅克看得出我没事。

column5: Just follow me, alright?\nI'll give you an update once we arrive.\nA {i}lot{/i} of stuff happened while you were out.
column6: 跟着我就好，行吗？\n到了之后我会把情况告诉你。\n你昏迷的时候发生了{i}很多{/i}事。

column5: Normally a statement like that, under these circumstances, would fill me with fear.{w}\nBut Damek says it with such a calm demeanor, that I'm led to believe everybody is fine.{w}\nHolding that optimism in my head, I smile as we make our way toward the shack he mentioned.
column6: 通常在这种情形下，这样的话会让我满心恐惧。{w}\n但达梅克说得那样平静，让我不禁相信大家都平安无事。{w}\n怀着这份乐观，我们朝他说的小屋走去，我微微一笑。

column5: Oh, you're awake. This is good.\nWhen we found you in the water, we were starting to worry.\nWe must ask — what happened? Last we checked, you were right behind us.
column6: 哦，你醒了。这很好。\n我们在水里找到你时，已经开始担心了。\n我们得问一句——发生了什么？我们最后看你时，你就在我们身后。

column5: I tell Howl exactly what happened. However, I tell him to keep it a secret.{w}\nI wouldn't want Damek to find out about Shane. He'd been hurt enough.
column6: 我把发生的事原原本本告诉了豪尔。不过，我让他保守秘密。{w}\n我不想让达梅克知道肖恩的事。他已经受够伤了。

column5: Interesting. Do not worry, we will keep your secret.\nIt is unfortunate how strong The Triumvirate's thrall can be.\nIf we win, at least no more good men will fall under their command.
column6: 有意思。别担心，我们会替你保守秘密。\n三人执政团的蛊惑竟能如此强大，实在不幸。\n如果我们赢了，至少不会再有好人沦为他们麾下。

column5: We've set up camp at a nearby shack. Follow us, please.\nI'll make sure to give you an update on everything once we're safe.\nA lot has happened while you were out, so there is much to talk about.
column6: 我们在附近的小屋扎了营。请跟我们来。\n等我们安全了，我一定把一切都告诉你。\n你昏迷时发生了很多事，有很多要谈。

column5: Normally a statement like that would fill me with fear, under these circumstances.{w}\nBut Howl says it with such a calm demeanor, that I'm led to believe everybody is fine.{w}\nHolding that optimism in my head, I smile as we make our way toward the shack he mentioned.
column6: 通常在这种情形下，这样的话会让我满心恐惧。{w}\n但豪尔说得那样平静，让我不禁相信大家都平安无事。{w}\n怀着这份乐观，我们朝他提到的那间小屋走去，我微微一笑。

column5: As soon as we arrive, I make my way to the shack, and lean against it.{w}\nWe barely even arrived in Balteus, and everything was already chaotic.{w}\nI don't know what I was expecting, so it's not exactly a surprise, either.
column6: 我们一到，我就走向小屋，靠在墙上。{w}\n我们才刚到巴尔泰乌斯，一切就已经乱成一团。{w}\n我不知道自己原本在期待什么，所以这也不算太意外。

column5: All of my comrades are scattered about, talking amongst themselves.{w}\nI'm glad that they survived. I try to account for them one by one as I look around.{w}\nAfter a few moments, something strikes me. I can't see either Fortaime or Valessa.
column6: 我的同伴们散落在各处，三三两两地交谈着。{w}\n我很高兴他们都活了下来。我环顾四周，试着一个个清点人数。{w}\n过了片刻，我忽然意识到一件事。福泰姆和瓦莱莎都不见踪影。

column5: Howl approaches me, and he lets out a sigh of relief.{w}\nI can imagine that my momentary disapperance stressed everybody out.
column6: 豪尔走近我，松了口气。{w}\n我能想象，我短暂的失踪让所有人都紧张不已。

column5: Good to see you, Monarch. We were worried.\nIt seems that almost everybody is accounted for.
column6: 见到你真好，君主。我们很担心。\n看来几乎所有人都平安归队了。

column5: I ask him where Valessa and Fortaime are.{w}\nHis demeanor quickly changes to that of sadness.
column6: 我问他瓦莱莎和福泰姆在哪里。{w}\n他的神情立刻变得悲伤。

column5: They are some of the few we have yet to find.\nBut we are certain that they live. We haven't found their bodies.\nMany of them washed ashore — casualties of the battle at sea.
column6: 他们是我们少数还没找到的人之一。\n但我们确信他们还活着。我们没找到他们的遗体。\n许多人被冲上岸——都是海战的伤亡者。

column5: We are relieved to know that you are not one of those casualties.\nThe plan is to wait in and around the shack until everybody shows up.\nThis might be a good time for you to get some more rest. Please relax.
column6: 得知你不是那些伤亡者之一，我们松了口气。\n计划是在小屋里和小屋附近等待，直到所有人都出现。\n也许现在正好适合你多休息一会儿。请放松些。

column5: Relax while my best friends are missing...?{w}\nThat was a tall order. I tell Howl that I might not be able to.
column6: 最好的朋友还下落不明，让我放松……？{w}\n这要求未免太高了。我告诉豪尔，我恐怕做不到。

column5: Please do not resort to worst case scenario thinking.\nThis is a time to be hopeful. We stand on the precipice of victory.\nWe will go and look for them personally. You deserve some rest.
column6: 请不要往最坏处想。\n现在是该抱有希望的时候。我们正站在胜利的边缘。\n我们会亲自去找他们。你该歇一歇了。

column5: Damek approcahes me, and he lets out a sigh of relief.{w}\nI can imagine that my momentary disappearance stressed everybody out.
column6: 达梅克走近我，松了口气。{w}\n我能想象，我短暂的失踪让所有人都紧张不已。

column5: Good to see you, Monarch. I was worried!\nAt least now, almost everybody is accounted for.
column6: 见到你真好，君主。我一直很担心！\n至少现在，几乎所有人都平安归队了。

column5: Almost everybody...? That worries me.{w}\nI ask him where Valessa and Fortaime are.
column6: 几乎所有人……？这让我担心起来。{w}\n我问他瓦莱莎和福泰姆在哪里。

column5: They're out there somewhere. We just can't find them.\nDon't worry. They're not dead. We haven't found their bodies.\nAnd trust me, we would have. A ton of them washed ashore...
column6: 他们就在外面某处。只是我们找不到。\n别担心。他们没死。我们没找到他们的遗体。\n相信我，要是他们死了，我们肯定找得到。好多人被冲上了岸……

column5: I'm just thankful that you didn't fall during the battle at sea.\nWe're just going to wait around this shack until everybody turns up.\nYou should probably use this time to relax. I know you couldn't before.
column6: 我只是庆幸你没有在海战中倒下。\n我们就守在这小屋附近，等所有人都出现。\n你大概该趁这时间放松一下。我知道你之前一直做不到。

column5: Relax while my best friends are missing...?{w}\nThat was a tall order. I tell Damek that I might not be able to.
column6: 最好的朋友还下落不明，让我放松……？{w}\n这要求未免太高了。我告诉达梅克，我恐怕做不到。

column5: Look, it's not a good idea to resort to negative thinking.\nWe stand on the verge of victory. This is a time to be hopeful.\nI'll go and look for them personally, okay? You should go and relax.
column6: 听着，往坏处想可不是好主意。\n我们正站在胜利的边缘。现在是该抱有希望的时候。\n我会亲自去找他们，好吗？你该去歇一歇。

column5: I nod, and thank him as I turn away.{w}\nScanning the area once more, I see who I can find.{w}\nA few of the comrades I can find slowly gather around me.
column6: 我点点头，道了谢，转身走开。{w}\n我又扫视了一圈，看看能找到谁。{w}\n我能找到的几位同伴慢慢聚到了我身边。

column5: Hey! Good to see that you're still among the living.\nThat was pretty intense, wasn't it? Sure scared me, at least.\nI'm not one for sailing, or fighting. So combining both? Yikes.
column6: 嘿！很高兴看到你还活着。\n那可真够刺激的，对吧？至少把我吓得不轻。\n我既不擅长航海，也不擅长打仗。两者凑一块儿？哎呀。

column5: Yeah, Pro was scared. Thankfully, I have strength for two.\nHe cowered in the corner while I did all of the hard work.
column6: 是啊，普洛吓坏了。幸好，我的力气能顶两个人。\n我干着所有苦活的时候，他缩在角落里。

column5: Did not...!
column6: 才没有……！

column5: Sure.
column6: 是啊。

column5: They share a quick laugh.{w}\nBut soon after that, I can tell that something is wrong.{w}\nIs there something that I'm not being told about all of this...?
column6: 他们相视一笑。{w}\n但很快，我就看出有什么不对劲。{w}\n是不是有什么事他们瞒着我……？

column5: It's about Alex, [firstname].\nHe's resting in the shack, in critical condition.\nI think we can nurse him back to health, but I'm not sure.
column6: 是关于亚历克斯，[firstname]。\n他正在小屋里休息，情况危急。\n我想我们能把他照料好，但我不确定。

column5: Oh, no...
column6: 哦，不……

column5: Look, it's probably best not to think about it too much.\nHe's in good hands. We just need to forge on as a team.\nIf it weren't for him, we'd all be dead at sea. This is a victory.
column6: 听着，最好别想太多。\n他有人照顾。我们只需要作为一个团队继续前进。\n要不是他，我们早就葬身大海了。这是一场胜利。

column5: I guess that's true.
column6: 我想这倒是真的。

column5: It was just important that we gave you a status report.\nI think once everybody gets here, we'll hold another meeting.\nOur strategy may need some adapting after these losses.
column6: 我们只是觉得该向你汇报一下情况。\n我想等所有人都到齐，我们会再开一次会。\n经历这些损失后，我们的策略也许需要做些调整。

column5: Yeah, go take a breather — you deserve it.\nRight now, our options are pretty limited.
column6: 是啊，去歇会儿吧——你应得的。\n目前，我们的选择相当有限。

column5: It's not ideal, but he's right. \nAll we can do right now is wait.\nThanks for the chat, [firstname].
column6: 这并不理想，但他说得对。\n我们现在能做的只有等待。\n谢谢你陪我们聊这些，[firstname]。

column5: I guess there wasn't much left for me to do.{w}\nI make my way to the shack, hopefully, to relax.{w}\nBut I was chasing an impossibility. I'd find no rest here.
column6: 我想我也没什么能做的了。{w}\n我朝小屋走去，希望能歇一歇。{w}\n但我追寻的只是一个不可能。在这里，我得不到安宁。

column5: Not until everything was over.{w}\nAnd that would mean we'd either win, or die.{w}\nAs I enter the shack, I pray that it's the former.
column6: 除非一切都结束。{w}\n而那意味着我们要么赢，要么死。{w}\n我走进小屋，祈祷会是前者。

column5: As soon as I'm inside, I let out a huge sigh.{w}\nThe emotions behind it are almost undiscernable.{w}\nThere was so much going on, my mind was overwhelmed.
column6: 一进屋，我就长长地叹了口气。{w}\n这声叹息背后的情绪几乎难以分辨。{w}\n发生的事情太多，我的脑子不堪重负。

column5: I guess I should take care of the important stuff first.{w}\nThe Pirate forces suffered heavy casualties, and Nada was almost lost.{w}\nI can see her resting on a small bed that sits in the corner of the shack.
column6: 我想我该先处理要紧的事。{w}\n海盗部队伤亡惨重，娜达也险些丧命。{w}\n我能看见她躺在那张摆在屋角的小床上。

column5: She notices me, and waves me over.{w}\nIt's a soft motion, and I can tell she's in pain.
column6: 她注意到了我，招手让我过去。{w}\n那动作很轻，我能看出她在忍痛。

column5: Hey. How're you holding up?
column6: 嘿。你还好吗？

column5: I tell her that I'm doing alright.
column6: 我告诉她我没事。

column5: At least that makes one of us.\nI almost died, but one of my men shielded me.\nThat's the weight of power, I guess. Watching them die.
column6: 至少我们之中还有一个人没事。\n我差点死了，但我的一名手下替我挡了下来。\n我想，这就是权力的重担吧。眼睁睁看着他们死去。

column5: She winces in pain, and I see a wound on her abdomen.
column6: 她痛得皱起脸，我看到她腹部有一道伤口。

column5: It never gets any easier, though.\nHey, can you promise me {i}one{/i} thing?
column6: 可这从来都不会变得容易些。\n嘿，你能答应我{i}一件{/i}事吗？

column5: I nod, and she waves me even closer, as her voice weakens.{w}\nShe holds out her hand, and I shake it with a firm grip.
column6: 我点点头，她的声音渐渐虚弱，招手让我再靠近些。{w}\n她伸出手，我紧紧握住。

column5: Give them {i}hell{/i} for me, [firstname].\nIf I die, I want to die knowing that we've won.\nShow them no quarter. They don't deserve it.
column6: 替我好好{i}收拾{/i}他们，[firstname]。\n如果我死了，我想知道自己死时我们已经赢了。\n别对他们手下留情。他们不配。

column5: I nod, and then release the grip on her hand.{w}\nShe dozes off into slumber, and I decide to leave her be.{w}\nRest would be important right now. She shouldn't force anything.
column6: 我点点头，然后松开了她的手。{w}\n她打起了盹，我决定不去打扰她。{w}\n此刻休息很重要。她不该勉强自己。

column5: After standing up, I look down at her.{w}\nIf it weren't for her, we wouldn't even be here right now.{w}\nI smile, and silently thank her for all that she's done.
column6: 站起身后，我低头看着她。{w}\n要不是她，我们现在根本不会在这里。{w}\n我微微一笑，默默感谢她所做的一切。

column5: I guess I should take care of the important stuff first.{w}\nThe Pirate forces suffered heavy casualties, and Alex was almost lost.{w}\nI can see him, resting on a small bed that sits in the corner of the shack.
column6: 我想我该先处理要紧的事。{w}\n海盗部队伤亡惨重，亚历克斯也险些丧命。{w}\n我能看见他躺在那张摆在屋角的小床上。

column5: He notices me, and waves me over.{w}\nIt's a soft motion, and I can tell he's in pain.
column6: 他注意到了我，招手让我过去。{w}\n那动作很轻，我能看出他在忍痛。

column5: Hey. How're you holding up?
column6: 嘿。你还好吗？

column5: I tell him that I'm doing alright.
column6: 我告诉他我没事。

column5: I can't believe that Nada fell during the battle.{w}\nI wanted to stop and mourn — but I knew that wasn't possible.{w}\nThese people deserved better, but the war dictated otherwise.
column6: 我无法相信娜达在战斗中倒下了。{w}\n我想停下来哀悼——但我知道那不可能。{w}\n这些人本该有更好的结局，但战争不由人。

column5: Perhaps after everything settled down, we could have a memorial.{w}\nNot just for Nada, but for everybody that was lost to this senseless war.{w}\nEspecially those lost in The Occupation. Everybody deserved a proper sendoff.
column6: 也许等一切平息之后，我们可以办一场追悼会。{w}\n不只是为娜达，而是为所有在这场无意义战争中逝去的人。{w}\n尤其是那些在占领中丧生的人。每个人都该有个体面的告别。

column5: I can't let this loss bring me down. I need to keep moving forward.{w}\nI promise myself that after this battle, I'll set aside time to grieve them all.{w}\nIt's just that right now, stopping to do that would likely end in my death.
column6: 我不能让这份失去击垮我。我得继续向前。{w}\n我向自己承诺，这场战斗之后，我会留出时间来哀悼他们所有人。{w}\n只是现在，停下来做这些很可能会让我丧命。

column5: The door to the shack swings open, startling me.{w}\nI turn around to see Gryz look around, oblivious to my presence.{w}\nAfter a few moments, he notices me, and lets out a nervous laugh.
column6: 小屋的门猛地被推开，吓了我一跳。{w}\n我转过身，看见格瑞兹四处张望，完全没注意到我。{w}\n过了一会儿，他看见了我，紧张地笑了一声。

column5: I never thought I'd see this place again.\nThis is where I used to live — before I joined The Triumvirate.\nA simple shepherd, that's all I was. They said they saw greatness in me.
column6: 我从没想过还能再见到这个地方。\n这里是我从前住的地方——在我加入三人执政团之前。\n我只是个普通的牧羊人。他们却说在我身上看到了不凡。

column5: But now I know that all they saw was a naive man, ready to serve.\nThey prey on the weak. On those whose minds can be warped.\nI'm a different man, now. But perhaps my change came too late.
column6: 但现在我知道，他们看到的只是一个天真、随时准备效忠的人。\n他们专挑弱者下手。专挑那些心智可以被扭曲的人。\n我现在已经不是从前那个人了。但也许我的转变来得太迟了。

column5: He steps forward and places his hands on the table.
column6: 他上前一步，双手按在桌上。

column5: I don't know if this is important or not, but Balteus has changed.\nIt used to be a beautiful place — but now, it's almost like it's dying.\nI can't put my finger on it, but something bad is happening here.
column6: 我不知道这重不重要，但巴尔泰乌斯变了。\n这里曾经是个美丽的地方——可现在，简直像在死去。\n我说不上来是怎么回事，但这里正发生着不好的事。

column5: So be careful, alright? We can't lose you, [firstname].\nBut if its within your power, I'd like to see Balteus restored.\nPlacing your throne here, and settling down, would be a good idea.
column6: 所以小心点，好吗？我们不能失去你，[firstname]。\n但如果这是你力所能及的，我希望能看到巴尔泰乌斯恢复旧貌。\n把你的王座设在这里，安顿下来，会是个好主意。

column5: I agree, even though I'm not entirely sure what he's talking about.{w}\nBalteus had changed? It's dying? I'm not sure how that works.{w}\nBut he's not one to lie, so I just let him continue talking.
column6: 我表示同意，尽管我不太明白他在说什么。{w}\n巴尔泰乌斯变了？它在死去？我不懂这怎么会。{w}\n但他不是个会撒谎的人，于是我由着他继续说下去。

column5: They made me kill my flock of sheep before joining them.\nThey said it symbolized the death of my old life, and the start of my new one.\nI felt awful, but I still chose to comply. I wasn't the smartest when I was younger.
column6: 加入他们之前，他们逼我杀光了我的羊群。\n他们说，这象征着我旧日生命的终结，和新生命的开始。\n我难受极了，却还是选择了顺从。我年轻时并不聪明。

column5: That's why I wear the skin of my favorite sheep. I called him Lassiter.\nI wore him as a tribute, but he slowly turned into a symbol of my resentment.\nSeeing him every day — that constant reminder — was part of why I defected.
column6: 所以我才披着我最爱的那只羊的皮。我叫他拉西特。\n我披着他是为了纪念，可他却渐渐变成了我怨恨的象征。\n每天看到他——那个不断的提醒——也是我叛离的原因之一。

column5: I couldn't live with what I did, so I sought redemption.\nOf course, you know the rest — so I won't bore you.\nThank you for listening to an old man's ramblings.
column6: 我无法带着自己做过的事活下去，于是寻求救赎。\n当然，后面的事你都知道——我就不啰嗦了。\n谢谢你听一个老头子絮叨。

column5: I give him my sympathy. That was an awful thing to experience.{w}\nThey used their status as \"Gods\" to manipulate young and impressionable people.{w}\nI can imagine that abandoning your moral code is easier if it's to impress \"Gods\" like them.
column6: 我向他表达了同情。那是段可怕的经历。{w}\n他们利用自己“神明”的身份，操纵年轻而易受影响的人。{w}\n我能想象，如果是为了讨好他们那样的“神明”，抛弃自己的道德准则会更容易些。

column5: I'm glad that he survived those tunnels, and chose to assist us in the final battle.{w}\nI make sure to tell him that, and he gives me a wide smile in exchange.
column6: 我很高兴他熬过了那些地道，并选择在最后的战斗中帮助我们。{w}\n我特意把这话告诉了他，他回赠给我一个大大的笑容。

column5: That means a lot. It really does.\nI want to see The Triumvirate fall, even if it means losing my life.\nGiving everybody out there a happy future? Now that would let me rest easy.
column6: 这对我意义重大。真的。\n我想看到三人执政团覆灭，哪怕要付出我的性命。\n给外面所有人一个幸福的未来？那才能让我安心。

column5: Of course, my survival would be preferable.\nI promise not to do anything too reckless. You have my word.\nThat's all I can really give you for now. I hope that it's enough.
column6: 当然，我更希望能活下来。\n我保证不会做太鲁莽的事。我向你保证。\n目前我能给你的也只有这些了。希望这就够了。

column5: He starts walking around the shack, inspecting things.{w}\nThere must be a lot of memories here, if this is where he used to live.{w}\nIt's probably best to leave him to himself, given the current circumstances.
column6: 他开始在小屋里走动，打量四周。{w}\n如果这里是他从前住的地方，那一定承载着许多回忆。{w}\n考虑到目前的情形，最好还是让他一个人待着。

column5: There isn't much left to do but rest, I suppose.
column6: 我想，除了休息，也没别的可做了。

column5: I move to the corner and press my back against the wall once more.{w}\nHopefully they're all able to find Valessa and Fortaime. I can't lose them now.{w}\nI'll rest in here for a while, and gather my bearings. This is not a time for freaking out.
column6: 我走到角落，再次把背靠在墙上。{w}\n但愿他们都能找到瓦莱莎和福泰姆。我现在不能失去他们。{w}\n我要在这儿歇一会儿，理清思绪。现在不是惊慌失措的时候。

column5: After a few hours of waiting, I almost can't handle it anymore.{w}\nIt's impossible for me to rest when my friends could be in danger.{w}\nMaking my way to the exit, I cross my fingers, hoping that things are okay.
column6: 等了几个小时后，我几乎再也受不了了。{w}\n朋友们可能身陷险境，我根本无法休息。{w}\n我朝出口走去，暗暗祈祷一切平安。

column5: Just as I'm about to leave, the door is swung open, catching me off guard.{w}\nI take a few steps back to avoid getting hit, letting out a sigh of relief afterwards.{w}\nIt's Ulric — but that's not all. A few moments after he enters, Valessa and Fortaime follow.
column6: 我正要离开，门突然被推开，让我猝不及防。{w}\n我后退几步以免被撞到，随后松了口气。{w}\n是乌尔里克——但不只他一个。他进来片刻之后，瓦莱莎和福泰姆也跟了进来。

column5: They're alive...!{w}\nWhat a huge relief this was!{w}\nAll the worry had taken its toll.
column6: 他们还活着……！{w}\n这真是让人大大松了口气！{w}\n之前的担忧早已让我身心俱疲。

column5: We hug each other, with big smiles on our faces.{w}\nFor a while there, I was scared of what might've happened.{w}\nThankfully, they're okay. I could rest easy as we move forward with everything.
column6: 我们露出大大的笑容，互相拥抱。{w}\n有一阵子，我很害怕可能出了什么事。{w}\n幸好他们没事。接下来的事，我也能安心些了。

column5: Sorry for taking a bit longer than you thought.\nWe've never been here before, so we got lost.
column6: 抱歉，比你想的久了一点。\n我们从没来过这里，所以迷路了。

column5: Yeah, and it was even harder because you're keeping quiet.\nIt's hard to find people who don't want to be found, you know?
column6: 是啊，而且你还瞒着我们，就更难了。\n不想被人找到的人，可不好找，你知道吗？

column5: I release the hug, and tell them that everything is fine.{w}\nI was worried — but I knew that they were capable of surviving.
column6: 我松开拥抱，告诉他们一切都好。{w}\n我担心过——但我知道他们有能力活下来。

column5: I can't believe how cold this place is.\nIt looks so uninviting, too. Scary, almost.
column6: 真不敢相信这地方这么冷。\n看起来也这么不友好。简直有点吓人。

column5: Yeah — hopefully we can change that.\nThe Triumvirate seems neglectful. But why...?
column6: 是啊——但愿我们能改变它。\n三人执政团似乎疏于治理。可为什么呢……？

column5: I shrug, unsure of how to answer that question.{w}\nWe're here to kill The Triumvirate, not reason with them.{w}\nI have a feeling this, among other questions, would remain unanswered.
column6: 我耸耸肩，不知该如何回答这个问题。{w}\n我们来这里是为了杀掉三人执政团，而不是跟他们讲道理。{w}\n我有种感觉，这个问题，还有许多其他问题，都会没有答案。

column5: Damek and Howl soon enter the shack.{w}\nFollowed by more of our comrades, we quickly fill the room.{w}\nGathering around the table, it's clear that it was time to plan.
column6: 达梅克和豪尔很快也进了小屋。{w}\n更多同伴紧随其后，房间里很快挤满了人。{w}\n大家围到桌旁，显然，是时候制定计划了。

column5: Alright, we need to talk about what happens next.\nUntil now, we've been pretty vague, since time was short.\nBut there's no more delaying. This is everything we've got.
column6: 好了，我们得谈谈接下来怎么办。\n到目前为止，因为时间紧迫，我们一直说得比较含糊。\n但不能再拖了。这就是我们手头所有的了。

column5: We need to push through the Town Square before anything can happen.\nBalteus is fortified by a large wall, so we can't get to the Library from the outside.\nThis means that the bulk of the battle will take place within the city itself.
column6: 行动开始前，我们必须先打通城镇广场。\n巴尔泰乌斯有一道高大的城墙，所以我们没法从外部抵达图书馆。\n这意味着大部分战斗都将在城内展开。

column5: However, we want to get to The Grand Library with as little resistance as possible.\nTo that end, we'll have our Monarch Vessels go in first, and cause a distraction.\nIf they can lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square, we can slip in.
column6: 不过，我们希望能尽可能少受阻碍地抵达大图书馆。\n为此，我们会先派君主容器进去制造混乱。\n如果能把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场，我们就能溜进去。

column5: However, we want to get to The Grand Library with as little resistance as possible.\nTo that end, we'll have our Created Seers go in first, and cause a distraction.\nIf they can lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square, we can slip in.
column6: 不过，我们希望能尽可能少受阻碍地抵达大图书馆。\n为此，我们会先派人造先知进去制造混乱。\n如果能把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场，我们就能溜进去。

column5: Since The Honor Guard can't enter the Library, it's perfect for a base of operations.\nLet's face it — this shack is dangerous — so we should get moving as soon as possible.\nOnce we're in the Library, we can relax, and prepare to launch our final assault.
column6: 既然荣誉卫队无法进入图书馆，那里就是理想的行动基地。\n说真的——这间小屋很危险——所以我们该尽快动身。\n一旦进了图书馆，我们就能放松下来，准备发动最后的攻势。

column5: The time has come for us to discuss what happens next.\nUntil now, and due to a lack of time, we spoke vaguely.\nBut we can delay no longer. This is what we have.
column6: 是时候讨论接下来怎么办了。\n到目前为止，由于时间不够，我们说得比较含糊。\n但我们不能再拖了。这就是我们所有的方案。

column5: We will need to push through The Town Square, to start things off.\nBalteus is fortified by a large wall, so we cannot get to the Library from the outside.\nThis means that the bulk of the battle will take place within the city itself.
column6: 行动开始时，我们需要先打通城镇广场。\n巴尔泰乌斯有一道高大的城墙，所以我们没法从外部抵达图书馆。\n这意味着大部分战斗都将在城内展开。

column5: However, we want to get to the library with as little resistance as possible.\nThis is why we will have our Monarch Vessels go in and cause a distraction.\nIf they can lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square, we can slip in.
column6: 不过，我们希望能尽可能少受阻碍地抵达图书馆。\n所以我们打算先派君主容器进去制造混乱。\n如果能把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场，我们就能溜进去。

column5: However, we want to get to the Library with as little resistance as possible.\nThis is why we will have our Created Seers go in and cause a distraction.\nIf they can lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square, we can slip in.
column6: 不过，我们希望能尽可能少受阻碍地抵达图书馆。\n所以我们打算先派人造先知进去制造混乱。\n如果能把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场，我们就能溜进去。

column5: The Honor Guard cannot enter the Library, so we will set up camp inside.\nThis shack is dangerous, so we should leave it as soon as we are able.\nOnce we're in the Library, we can relax, and prepare our final assault.
column6: 荣誉卫队无法进入图书馆，所以我们会把营地设在里面。\n这间小屋很危险，所以只要能走，我们就该尽快离开。\n一旦进了图书馆，我们就能放松下来，准备最后的攻势。

column5: And what will that final assault consist of...?
column6: 那最后的攻势具体要做什么……？

column5: Good question. \nHere's what we've been thinking.\nIf the floor is mine, I'll reveal our plan.
column6: 问得好。\n我们是这样构想的。\n既然轮到我发言，那我就把计划说出来吧。

column5: Howl nods, giving Damek the floor. He steps forward.{w}\nPlacing a scroll on the table, he promptly unfolds it.{w}\nI can see that it's a map of Balteus. The entire city.
column6: 豪尔点点头，把发言权交给达梅克。他上前一步。{w}\n他把一卷羊皮纸放在桌上，随即展开。{w}\n我看出那是巴尔泰乌斯的地图。整座城。

column5: Everybody gathers around the table, putting aside any other business.{w}\nIf the strategy at sea was any indication, I know this operation is in good hands.{w}\nThey certainly seem to know what they're doing. I can feel our morale rising.
column6: 众人围到桌旁，暂且放下其他一切。{w}\n如果海上的策略能说明什么，那我知道这次行动交对了人。{w}\n他们显然知道自己在做什么。我能感觉到士气在上升。

column5: We are glad that you asked.\nHere is a bit of what we've been thinking.\nDamek, would you be so kind as to reveal our plan?
column6: 很高兴你问这个。\n这是我们构想的一部分。\n达梅克，能否劳烦你把计划说出来？

column5: Damek nods, and steps forward.{w}\nPlacing a scroll on the table, he promptly unfolds it.{w}\nI can see that it's a map of Balteus. The entire city.
column6: 达梅克点点头，上前一步。{w}\n他把一卷羊皮纸放在桌上，随即展开。{w}\n我看出那是巴尔泰乌斯的地图。整座城。

column5: Everybody gathers around the table, putting aside any other business.{w}\nIf the strategy at sea was any indication, I know this operation is in good hands.{w}\nThey certainly seem to know what they're doing. I can feel our morale rising.
column6: 众人围到桌旁，暂且放下其他一切。{w}\n如果海上的策略能说明什么，那我知道这次行动交对了人。{w}\n他们显然知道自己在做什么。我能感觉到士气在上升。

column5: He starts to speak with certainty and confidence.{w}\nIt's impressive. They must've been planning this for a while.{w}\nWe all watch intently, curious to see what kind of strategy they have.
column6: 他开始带着笃定和自信讲了起来。{w}\n这令人钦佩。他们一定筹划了很久。{w}\n我们都专注地看着，好奇他们有什么样的策略。

column5: This is the main area of the city.\nOur goal is to ensure that [firstname] has a clear path to the castle.\nThat way, he can slip inside and kill The Triumvirate with minimal effort.
column6: 这里是城市的主要区域。\n我们的目标是确保[firstname]有一条通往城堡的畅通之路。\n这样，他就能溜进去，以最小的代价杀掉三人执政团。

column5: This is the main area of the city.\nOur goal is to ensure that [firstname] has a clear path to the castle.\nThat way, she can slip inside and kill The Triumvirate with minimal effort.
column6: 这里是城市的主要区域。\n我们的目标是确保[firstname]有一条通往城堡的畅通之路。\n这样，她就能溜进去，以最小的代价杀掉三人执政团。

column5: Howl and myself will lure The Honor Guard to the Town Square.\nThis is where the bulk of the battle will take place. It shouldn't be too hard.\nWith the added might of our Draconic allies, we'll have no problem at all.
column6: 我和豪尔会把荣誉卫队引到城镇广场。\n大部分战斗将在那里展开。应该不会太难。\n有了我们龙族盟友的助力，我们完全不成问题。

column5: Pro will sneak away from the Town Square, and infiltrate the castle.\nHis job will be to cause a distraction, luring enemies away from the atrium.\nWith that done, the rest should be smooth sailing for [firstname].
column6: 普洛会从城镇广场悄悄离开，潜入城堡。\n他的任务是制造混乱，把敌人从中庭引开。\n只要做到这点，剩下的事对[firstname]来说就该一帆风顺了。

column5: I'll go with Pro, if that's okay with you.\nI know the layout of the castle, and he'll need some backup.\nWe can't expect him to hold off an entire horde of suits at once.
column6: 如果你不介意，我跟普洛一起去。\n我熟悉城堡的布局，而且他需要有人接应。\n我们不能指望他一个人挡住一整群铠甲兵。

column5: Very well. Gryz will accompany Pro.\nThe two of them will have no problem clearing the castle.\nThe bulk of The Honor Guard will be with me in the Town Square.
column6: 很好。格瑞兹会和普洛同行。\n他们俩清理城堡不会有问题。\n荣誉卫队的主力会和我一起待在城镇广场。

column5: Sounds like a piece of cake, to be honest.\nConsider that castle empty upon your arrival!\nCausing distractions is totally a specialty of mine.
column6: 说实话，听起来小菜一碟。\n你就当到的时候城堡已经空了吧！\n制造混乱可是我的拿手好戏。

column5: Alright. That takes care of Howl, Pro, and myself.\nThe rest of you will accompany [firstname] to the castle.\nLet's see here, I should have another map detailing our current area.
column6: 好。豪尔、普洛和我都安排好了。\n其余的人会陪[firstname]去城堡。\n让我看看，我应该还有一张标注我们当前区域的地图。

column5: The only way to approach The Triumvirate's castle is directly from the front.\nThat is — unless you know a secret or two. This involves a hidden mountain pass.
column6: 接近三人执政团城堡的唯一方式，就是从正面过去。\n除非——你知道一两个秘密。这涉及一条隐蔽的山道。

column5: Using this pass, you can go {i}around{/i} Balteus.\nIt'll be much easier than sneaking through the city.\nJoining you will be Ulric, Fortaime, and Valessa.
column6: 走这条山道，你们就能{i}绕过{/i}巴尔泰乌斯。\n这比偷偷穿过城市要容易得多。\n乌尔里克、福泰姆和瓦莱莎会与你们同行。

column5: Damek — if you'd let me join them, I could help out.\nRemember who tipped you off about this hidden trail...?\nI can even use The Blade of Exodus if [firstname] is in a bind.
column6: 达梅克——如果你让我加入他们，我能帮上忙。\n还记得是谁告诉你这条隐秘山路的吗……？\n如果[firstname]陷入困境，我甚至能使用流亡之刃。

column5: Alright, sure. I have no problem with that.\nSovy will accompany the group headed to the castle.\nThey'll split up when they get close. Let's see here.
column6: 好，没问题。我不反对。\n索维会和前往城堡的那组同行。\n靠近之后他们会分头行动。让我看看。

column5: How did you learn about this trail, Damek?\nCan you be certain that it's not a trap?
column6: 你是怎么知道这条山道的，达梅克？\n你能确定这不是陷阱吗？

column5: Yeah, I'm certain. It came from Gryz's files.\nIf there's anyone I trust about this nation, it's him.
column6: 能，我确定。这是从格瑞兹的文件里得来的。\n要说这个国家的事，我最信任的就是他。

column5: Alright, fair enough.\nSo the four of us will take the trail to the castle.
column6: 好吧，有道理。\n那我们四个就走山道去城堡。

column5: Not all the way, I'm afraid.\nI'll need some of you to split up on the way.\nThere's another map here. Just a second.
column6: 恐怕不能一路同行。\n路上我需要你们中的一些人分头行动。\n这里还有一张地图。等一下。

column5: You should emerge from the mountain pass right beside the castle.\nBecause of all the distractions, your path inside should be clear.\nBut I need Fortaime to do something special for us first.
column6: 你们从山道出来时，应该正好在城堡旁边。\n由于那些混乱，你们进城的路线应该畅通无阻。\n但我需要福泰姆先为我们做一件特别的事。

column5: Me...? Special?\nWhat do you need me to do?
column6: 我……？特别的事？\n你需要我做什么？

column5: I'll have you climb the castle, scaling the outside walls.\nYour job will be to get inside, and ring the bell of retreat.\nIf you can find it, it should make The Honor Guard stand down.
column6: 我要你攀上城堡，翻过外墙。\n你的任务是进入内部，敲响撤退的钟。\n只要你能找到它，应该就能让荣誉卫队停手。

column5: Wait, seriously...?\nAll of them?
column6: 等等，你是认真的……？\n他们全部？

column5: Yeah, all of them.\nI'm putting a lot of trust in you, here.\nDo you think you can do this for us?
column6: 对，全部。\n我在这儿可是把很大的信任交给了你。\n你觉得能替我们做到吗？

column5: Of course...!\nClimbing is my specialty.\nI'll have that bell ringing in no time.
column6: 当然……！\n攀爬可是我的专长。\n我马上就能让那口钟响起来。

column5: Good.
column6: 很好。

column5: The rest of you will enter the castle from the front.\nAgain, your path should be clear if all goes as planned.\nIf not — well, you'll have to fight your way through. But I believe in you.
column6: 其余的人从正面进入城堡。\n再说一次，如果一切按计划进行，你们的路线应该畅通。\n如果不行——那你们就只能一路打进去了。但我相信你们。

column5: Sounds good to me.
column6: 我没问题。

column5: Yeah, we can do this — no problem.
column6: 是啊，我们能行——没问题。

column5: Glad to hear it.
column6: 听你这么说我很高兴。

column5: That is all we've come up with.\nDoes everybody find it acceptable...?
column6: 这就是我们想出的全部方案。\n大家都觉得可以接受吗……？

column5: Everybody nods, knowing their part.{w}\nIt seemed like they had almost thought of it all.{w}\nWith a strategy like that, victory seems almost certain.
column6: 每个人都点头，清楚自己的角色。{w}\n他们似乎几乎把一切都想到了。{w}\n有这样的策略，胜利几乎已是板上钉钉。

column5: As long as I could defeat The Triumvirate and that idol.{w}\nEven if everybody plays their part — the end is still all on me.{w}\nI'd do my best not to let them down. But part of me is filled with fright.
column6: 只要我能击败三人执政团和那尊灵像。{w}\n即使每个人都各司其职——最后的成败仍全在我身上。{w}\n我会尽全力不让他们失望。但我心里有一部分充满了恐惧。

column5: Alright, let's go outside.\nWe'll head to The Grand Library as a group.\nIf we can get in there without trouble, the rest will be easy.
column6: 好，我们出去吧。\n我们全队一起前往大图书馆。\n只要能顺利进去，剩下的就简单了。

column5: The Monarch Vessels should make it pretty easy for us.{w}\nThey'll lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square.{w}\nIf they can do that, then we can slip in pretty much undetected.
column6: 君主容器应该能让我们轻松不少。{w}\n他们会把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场。{w}\n只要做到这点，我们就能神不知鬼不觉地溜进去。

column5: The Created Seers should make is pretty easy for us.{w}\nThey'll lure The Honor Guard away from the Town Square.{w}\nIf they can do that, then we can slip in pretty much undetected.
column6: 人造先知应该能让我们轻松不少。{w}\n他们会把荣誉卫队引离城镇广场。{w}\n只要做到这点，我们就能神不知鬼不觉地溜进去。

column5: Hopefully they could survive the task.{w}\nThis operation would be divided into two phases, then.{w}\nTake The Grand Library. Then Take The Triumvirate's Castle.
column6: 但愿他们能在这场任务中活下来。{w}\n那么，这次行动将分为两个阶段。{w}\n拿下大图书馆。再拿下三人执政团的城堡。

column5: With everything planned, and out in the open, we exit the shack.{w}\nHope fills the air, for the first time in a while. We could do this.{w}\nI smile at my comrades as we head outside, one by one.
column6: 一切已筹划妥当，也和盘托出，我们走出了小屋。{w}\n久违地，空气中充满了希望。我们能行。{w}\n我们一个接一个地走出去，我对同伴们笑了笑。

column5: The cold, uninviting air assaults me as soon as I exit the shack.{w}\nIt's like Eastcrown. I'm not sure how people could survive in this place.{w}\nWell, not that there's many people here. It's mainly those suits of armor.
column6: 一出小屋，寒冷而不友好的空气就扑面而来。{w}\n就像东冠一样。我不知道人们怎么能在这地方活下来。{w}\n不过，这里本来也没多少人。主要都是那些铠甲兵。

column5: I can hear everybody talking — going over the roles they were assigned.{w}\nIf everybody did what they were supposed to do, then we'd win this for sure.{w}\nOf course, as long as I could destroy The Triumvirate and that idol they're housing.
column6: 我能听见大家在交谈——复述各自被分配的任务。{w}\n如果每个人都做好分内之事，那我们一定能赢。{w}\n当然，前提是我能摧毁三人执政团和他们供奉的那尊灵像。

column5: Sneak into the castle — and lure everybody away from the main atrium.\nSeems pretty easy to me. [firstname] will have no resistance at all.
column6: 潜入城堡——把所有人从主中庭引开。\n在我看来挺简单的。[firstname]将不会遇到任何抵抗。

column5: And if I can ring that bell, then everybody will be safe...!\nAll those years of climbing has finally paid off. This is gonna be great.
column6: 只要我能敲响那口钟，大家就都安全了……！\n这么多年爬来爬去，总算派上用场了。这一定会很棒。

column5: Ulric is quick to interject, putting any arrogance to rest before it can blossom.
column6: 乌尔里克立刻插话，把任何可能滋生的自满都扼杀在萌芽中。

column5: Look — none of that is going to happen if we can't take The Grand Library.\nWe need to establish a foothold. A safe place to retreat to if things go south.
column6: 听着——如果我们拿不下大图书馆，那些都不会发生。\n我们需要建立据点。一个万一情况不妙时能撤退的安全之处。

column5: They all nod, and stop the discussion they were having.{w}\nIt's true, though. Without haven, we're out in the open, completely unsafe.{w}\nAt least the first phase of our plan wasn't too complicated. I know we'd seize the library.
column6: 他们都点点头，停止了刚才的讨论。{w}\n不过，这是事实。没有避难所，我们就暴露在外，毫无安全可言。{w}\n至少计划的第一阶段不算太复杂。我知道我们能拿下图书馆。

column5: I notice that one of our comrades is carrying Alex.{w}\nThat's good. The Library would be the best place for him to get rest.{w}\nHe's fast asleep, which is pretty surprising. He must be a heavy sleeper.
column6: 我注意到一名同伴正背着亚历克斯。{w}\n这很好。图书馆会是让他休息的最佳之处。{w}\n他睡得很沉，这挺让人意外的。他一定睡得很死。

column5: I notice that one of our comrades is carrying Nada.{w}\nThat's good. The Library would be the best place for her to get rest.{w}\nShe's fast asleep, which is pretty surprising. She must be a heavy sleeper.
column6: 我注意到一名同伴正背着娜达。{w}\n这很好。图书馆会是让她休息的最佳之处。{w}\n她睡得很沉，这挺让人意外的。她一定睡得很死。

column5: The city should only be a couple of hours away.\nWe trust that you can all handle the cold...?
column6: 离城里应该只有几个小时的路程了。\n我们相信你们都能扛得住这寒冷……？

column5: We don't really have much of a choice, Howl.\nLet's get going. I think our goal is pretty clear.
column6: 我们其实没什么选择，豪尔。\n走吧。我想我们的目标已经很清楚了。

column5: Upon hearing that, we all start walking toward the city.{w}\nI can see the impressive wall that surrounds everything. It's beautiful.{w}\nHowever, I can't see anything past it. I have no idea what Balteus looks like.
column6: 听到这话，我们全都朝城里走去。{w}\n我能看见环绕着一切的宏伟城墙。很美。{w}\n然而，墙后什么也看不见。我完全不知道巴尔泰乌斯是什么样子。

column5: We walk through thick layers of snow, and my legs start to tire out.{w}\nBut I'm not in a position where I have any choice. Pushing forward is mandatory.{w}\nAfter what feels like a small eternity, we finally arrive at the gates leading into Balteus.
column6: 我们穿过厚厚的积雪，我的双腿开始酸痛。{w}\n但我没有选择的余地。必须向前。{w}\n仿佛过了漫长的一个世纪，我们终于到达了通往巴尔泰乌斯的城门。

column5: The town gates, and the wall, are an amazing sight.{w}\nIntricate details are carved into the stone. It's a work of art.{w}\nSomething told me The Monarchy made this. Not The Triumvirate.
column6: 城门和城墙，景象令人叹为观止。{w}\n石头上雕刻着繁复的纹样。这是一件艺术品。{w}\n我隐约觉得这是君主国所建。不是三人执政团。

column5: This looks amazing...!\nThis must be a remnant of The Monarchy, right?\nThe Triumvirate can't be {i}this{/i} artistic. I know it.
column6: 这看起来太惊人了……！\n这一定是君主国留下的遗迹，对吧？\n三人执政团可没{i}这么{/i}有艺术品味。我知道。

column5: Correct. This looks just as we remember it.\nHowever, Balteus wasn't always this cold.\nSomething bad has happened to the nation.
column6: 没错。这和我们记忆中的一模一样。\n然而，巴尔泰乌斯并非一直这么寒冷。\n这个国家发生了不好的事。

column5: Oh, I see. \nLike what?
column6: 哦，我明白了。\n比如什么？

column5: We're not sure.\nHowever, it is probably due to The Triumvirate.\nIt pains us to see how much they've defiled our former home.
column6: 我们也不确定。\n不过，这大概要归咎于三人执政团。\n看到他们如此玷污我们昔日的家园，我们很痛心。

column5: We used to live in Balteus. It housed the throne, and our ruler.\nTo see it reduced to a frozen wasteland? It is almost too much to bear.\nLet us head inside. We need to see what else has changed over the years.
column6: 我们曾在巴尔泰乌斯生活。那里安放着王座，还有我们的统治者。\n看着它沦为一片冰封的荒原？这几乎让人无法承受。\n我们进去吧。我们得看看这些年来还有什么变了。

column5: It reminds me of what we thought would happen to Valinorth.{w}\nWithout the spirit idol, it'd wither away and freeze over like Eastcrown.{w}\nWe have since learned that was false — but what's happened to Balteus, then?
column6: 这让我想起我们曾以为瓦利诺斯会遭遇的事。{w}\n没有灵像，它就会像东冠一样凋敝、冰封。{w}\n后来我们知道那是错的——那巴尔泰乌斯究竟出了什么事？

column5: As we all start to make our way inside the city, Damek stops us.{w}\nHe looks a bit worried, and I can tell that he's lost in deep thought.
column6: 我们正要进城，达梅克叫住了我们。{w}\n他看起来有些担忧，我能看出他正陷入沉思。

column5: Seers...? Please come forth.
column6: 先知们……？请上前来。

column5: A few moments later, a group of our Seers step forward.
column6: 片刻之后，一群先知走上前来。

column5: We don't have much time to waste.\nAs soon as we get inside, you need to get to work.\nLure The Honor Guard away from our path. Understood?
column6: 我们没多少时间可浪费。\n我们一进去，你们就得开始行动。\n把荣誉卫队从我们的路线上引开。明白吗？

column5: Of course. Your path to the Library will be clear.\nAfter the fighting dies down, we will come and join you.\nIt should be easy, so don't expect us to be too far behind.
column6: 当然。通往图书馆的路会为你们清空。\n战斗平息之后，我们会来与你们会合。\n这应该不难，所以别指望我们落在后面太久。

column5: Yes, of course. Thank you very much.\nLet's see — is there anything else to cover?
column6: 好，当然。非常感谢。\n让我看看——还有什么要交代的吗？

column5: Monarch Vessels...? Where are you?
column6: 君主容器……？你们在哪儿？

column5: A few moments later, a group of our Monarch Vessels step forward.
column6: 片刻之后，一群君主容器走上前来。

column5: We don't have much time to waste.\nAs soon as we get inside, you need to get to work.\nLure The Honor Guard away from our path. Understood?
column6: 我们没多少时间可浪费。\n我们一进去，你们就得开始行动。\n把荣誉卫队从我们的路线上引开。明白吗？

column5: Yes, of course. Your path to the Library will be clear.\nAs soon as the fighting dies down, we will come and join you.\nThis should be easy, so don't expect us to be too far behind.
column6: 是的，当然。通往图书馆的路会为你们清空。\n战斗一平息，我们就来与你们会合。\n这应该不难，所以别指望我们落在后面太久。

column5: Yes, of course. Thank you very much.\nLet's see — is there anything else to cover?
column6: 好，当然。非常感谢。\n让我看看——还有什么要交代的吗？

column5: He turns back to face the rest of the group.{w}\nGulping, it's clear that he's fraught with anxiety.
column6: 他转过身，面向其余的人。{w}\n他咽了口唾沫，显然满心焦虑。

column5: Look. We're about to do something that's never been done before.\nWe're seizing territory from The Triumvirate, right under their noses.\nMuch like they did to Mazeo — we're about to occupy Balteus.
column6: 听着。我们即将做一件前所未有的事。\n我们要在三人执政团的眼皮底下夺取他们的地盘。\n就像他们当初对马泽奥所做的那样——我们即将占领巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: But that does {i}not{/i} mean we are like them.\nWe do what we do, in order to gain our freedom.\nThey occupied Mazeo, wanting to oppress us even further.
column6: 但这{i}绝不{/i}意味着我们和他们一样。\n我们这么做，是为了赢得自由。\n他们占领马泽奥，是想进一步压迫我们。

column5: We all exchange glances, and nod at one another.
column6: 我们彼此交换眼神，互相点头。

column5: I want you to all remember that as we press forward:\nWar can blur the lines between good and evil — but I know where we stand.\nIf you know that too, then there's nothing that can stop you. You are heroes.
column6: 我希望你们在前进时都记住这一点：\n战争会模糊善恶的界限——但我知道我们站在哪一边。\n如果你们也清楚，那就没有什么能阻挡你们。你们是英雄。

column5: With nothing left to say, we slowly make our way into the city.{w}\nI can tell that due to Damek's encouraging words, everybody is happy.{w}\nHowever, as we enter, nothing prepares us for the sight that awaits us.
column6: 再没什么可说的了，我们缓缓走进城中。{w}\n我能看出，因为达梅克那番鼓舞人心的话，大家都很振奋。{w}\n然而，当我们进城时，眼前的景象让我们毫无准备。

column5: Howl immediately steps forward, taking in the sight before him.{w}\nBalteus looks almost uninhabitable. It's in a state of decay, and death.{w}\nI know The Honor Guard doesn't need a paradise — but this is crazy.
column6: 豪尔立刻上前一步，打量着眼前的景象。{w}\n巴尔泰乌斯看上去几乎已不适合居住。一片衰败、死寂的景象。{w}\n我知道荣誉卫队不需要天堂——但这太离谱了。

column5: What have they done...?
column6: 他们都干了什么……？

column5: It's clear that Howl is hurt. This used to be The Monarchy's home, after all.{w}\nHopefully there would be a way to reverse all of this. It isn't right.
column6: 显然豪尔很受伤。毕竟这里曾是君主国的家园。{w}\n但愿有办法逆转这一切。这不对。

column5: This is... Well, I certainly didn't expect this.\nI'm guessing it didn't look like this in your time?
column6: 这……嗯，我确实没料到会这样。\n我猜在你们的时代，它可不是这个样子？

column5: No. Balteus was a paradise.\nThis is unacceptable, Damek.\nWe must find a way to fix it.
column6: 不是。巴尔泰乌斯曾是一座天堂。\n这不可接受，达梅克。\n我们必须找到办法修复它。

column5: Of course. There's no way I'll let this stand.\nIt's a bit of a shock, but our plan remains unchanged.\nSecure The Grand Library, then kill The Triumvirate.
column6: 当然。我绝不会坐视不管。\n这确实令人震惊，但我们的计划不变。\n拿下大图书馆，然后杀掉三人执政团。

column5: After he's done talking, we see a horde of Honor Guard suits walk by.{w}\nWe quickly run off to the side and hide behind a nearby building.{w}\nI've never seen anything like this. The building is pitch black.
column6: 他说完后，我们看到一大群荣誉卫队铠甲兵走过。{w}\n我们赶紧跑到一旁，躲进附近一栋建筑后面。{w}\n我从没见过这样的东西。那建筑漆黑一片。

column5: Pieces of it crumble off, almost like it's been burnt or charred.{w}\nBut it hasn't. I know a building can't die, but there's no other way to put it.{w}\nLike its source of life has been cut off, it appears to be living on borrowed time.
column6: 碎片不断剥落，就像被烧焦或炭化过一样。{w}\n但其实没有。我知道建筑不会死，但实在没有别的说法。{w}\n仿佛生命的源头被切断，它像是在苟延残喘。

column5: What's going on, here...?
column6: 这里到底怎么了……？

column5: This is disgusting. Look.
column6: 这真恶心。你看。

column5: He looks down, and we all look at his feet.{w}\nWe're no longer standing in snow, but ash and \"soot\".{w}\nI start to wonder if it was ever really snowing at all.
column6: 他低下头，我们也看向他的脚下。{w}\n我们踩的不再是雪，而是灰烬和“煤烟”。{w}\n我开始怀疑，之前究竟有没有下过雪。

column5: This is Alestia's fate, if we leave it in their hands.\nThey don't care about the land. They only care about themselves.\nThis is proof enough that we're on the right side of history.
column6: 如果我们把事情交给他们，这就是阿莱斯蒂亚的命运。\n他们不在乎这片土地。他们只在乎自己。\n这足以证明，我们站在历史正确的一边。

column5: Howl turns to me, and places a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 豪尔转向我，把手搭在我的肩上。

column5: We suspect that this may be related to their \"dark idol\".\nMonarch, above all else, please prioritize its destruction.
column6: 我们怀疑这可能与他们的“黑暗灵像”有关。\n君主，无论如何，请务必优先摧毁它。

column5: I nod, as previous visions start to repeat themselves in my mind.{w}\nI was facing that idol, with the blade. Everything is coming to pass.{w}\nAfter our short talk, our attention is directed back toward The Honor Guard.
column6: 我点点头，过往的幻象开始在脑海中重现。{w}\n我手持那把剑，面对着那尊灵像。一切都在应验。{w}\n简短交谈之后，我们的注意力又转回了荣誉卫队身上。

column5: Monarch Vessels? Come here.\nI think this is our best chance to take action.\nIf that group is gone, our path to the Library is clear.
column6: 君主容器？过来。\n我想这是我们行动的最好机会。\n只要那群人离开，我们通往图书馆的路就畅通了。

column5: Upon hearing this, they quickly group up in front of Damek.{w}\nOur goal of seizing The Grand Library seems pretty attainable.
column6: 听到这话，他们迅速在达梅克面前集合。{w}\n我们夺取大图书馆的目标看来相当可行。

column5: Yes, sir. It should be easy enough to take them down.\nAfter they're dealt with, we'll meet you all in the Library.
column6: 是，长官。解决他们应该不难。\n处理完他们，我们就在图书馆与你们会合。

column5: Good. Go around this building and attack from the other side.\nThey'll be focusing on you, so we'll head in the opposite direction.
column6: 好。绕过这栋建筑，从另一侧发动攻击。\n他们会把注意力放在你们身上，我们就往相反的方向去。

column5: Perfect. Then see you at the Library.\nIf we don't make it — it's been an honor.
column6: 太好了。那就在图书馆见。\n如果我们没能到——能与你们并肩，是我的荣幸。

column5: After exchanging a nod, both groups part ways.{w}\nThe Monarch Vessels prepare to distract The Honor Guard.{w}\nDamek points to a nearby road, signalling where we should run.
column6: 互相点头之后，两队人马分道扬镳。{w}\n君主容器准备去引开荣誉卫队。{w}\n达梅克指向附近一条路，示意我们该往那儿跑。

column5: The Grand Library is right over there.\nWe'll run on my mark, so just hold on.
column6: 大图书馆就在那边。\n听我口令就跑，先稳住。

column5: After speaking, he immediately places a finger against his mouth.{w}\nIt's clear that we need to remain silent while the Vessels carry out their goal.{w}\nWe wait there in an intense silence, waiting to hear the clashing of swords.
column6: 说完，他立刻把一根手指按在唇上。{w}\n显然，在容器们执行任务时，我们必须保持安静。{w}\n我们在死一般的寂静中等待着，等着听见刀剑相交的声音。

column5: We all stare at each other, in unease.{w}\nWe know that when they start to fight, some of them may die.{w}\nIt pains me that sacrifice was necessary in order to attain our goal.
column6: 我们不安地互相望着。{w}\n我们知道，一旦他们开战，其中一些人可能会死。{w}\n为了实现目标竟必须牺牲，这让我很痛心。

column5: But I know that their sacrifice would never be forgotten.{w}\nMy heart sinks as soon as I hear them start to fight.{w}\nI hear screaming, and steel against steel.
column6: 但我知道，他们的牺牲绝不会被遗忘。{w}\n一听见他们开打，我的心就沉了下去。{w}\n我听见尖叫，还有钢铁相击的声音。

column5: My instinct tells me to run immediately, but Damek has yet to move.{w}\nI can see him wince every time the skirmish gets a little louder.{w}\nBut soon enough, he makes the call, and we're all running.
column6: 本能让我立刻就跑，但达梅克还没有动。{w}\n每当那边的交锋声稍微变大，我都能看到他皱眉。{w}\n但很快，他下达了号令，我们全都跑了起来。
